import os

# Output text file name
OUTPUT_FILE = "plain_txt.txt"

# File extensions to include in the dump
ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS = {
    ".ts", ".tsx", ".js", ".jsx", ".json", ".css", 
    ".scss", ".html", ".md", ".py", ".sql", ".prisma"
}

# Directories to skip completely
IGNORE_DIRS = {
    "node_modules",
    ".git",
    ".next",
    "dist",
    "build",
    "coverage",
    ".idea",
    ".vscode",
    "__pycache__",
    "public", # remove if you want asset files listed
}

# Specific files to ignore
IGNORE_FILES = {
    OUTPUT_FILE,
    "generate_dump.py",
    "package-lock.json",
    "yarn.lock",
    "pnpm-lock.yaml",
    ".DS_Store",
}

def generate_code_dump():
    project_root = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
    output_path = os.path.join(project_root, OUTPUT_FILE)
    
    file_count = 0

    with open(output_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as outfile:
        outfile.write("==================================================\n")
        outfile.write("           PROJECT SOURCE CODE DUMP               \n")
        outfile.write("==================================================\n\n")

        for root, dirs, files in os.walk(project_root):
            # Exclude ignored directories in-place
            dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in IGNORE_DIRS]

            for file in sorted(files):
                if file in IGNORE_FILES:
                    continue

                ext = os.path.splitext(file)[1].lower()
                if ext not in ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS:
                    continue

                full_path = os.path.join(root, file)
                rel_path = os.path.relpath(full_path, project_root)

                outfile.write(f"\n{'=' * 60}\n")
                outfile.write(f"FILE: {rel_path}\n")
                outfile.write(f"{'=' * 60}\n\n")

                try:
                    with open(full_path, "r", encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as infile:
                        outfile.write(infile.read())
                        outfile.write("\n")
                    file_count += 1
                except Exception as e:
                    outfile.write(f"/* Error reading file: {e} */\n")

    print(f"Success! Aggregated {file_count} files into '{OUTPUT_FILE}'.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    generate_code_dump()

﻿# Bee's Hive - Restaurant Management System

A modern restaurant management application built with React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. Supports three roles: Admin, Waiter, and Supervisor.

## Roles

| Role | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Admin** | Full restaurant management - tables, menu, staff, orders, inventory, payments, analytics |
| **Waiter** | Table allocation, session management, order creation, tokens/KOT, order status tracking |
| **Supervisor** | Menu management, order preparation, inventory, purchase requests |

## Features

### Admin
- Dashboard with real-time analytics
- Table management grouped area-wise (Indoor, Garden, Terrace, ...) — add, edit, deactivate
- Menu management (create categories, dishes with images)
- Staff management (create/administer admins, waiters and supervisors)
- Order monitoring
- Bill generation and payment processing (CASH, UPI, PHONE UPI, DEBIT CARD, CREDIT CARD, QR CODE, WALLET)
- Receipt printing (DIVYE PT-210 #2 — Admin printer)
- Reprint bills
- Inventory management
- Purchase request approval
- Payment history
- Analytics (revenue, orders, averages)

### Waiter
- Table floor view grouped area-wise (Indoor, Garden, ...) with real-time status
- Dining session management
- Order creation with menu browsing
- Today's Specials highlighting
- Token/KOT printing for kitchen
- Order status tracking

### Supervisor
- Menu management (create categories, dishes with images)
- Dish image upload
- Today's Specials management
- Order board (New → Preparing → Ready)
- Inventory tracking
- Purchase request creation

## Development Setup

### Prerequisites
- Node.js 18+
- npm or yarn

### Installation

```bash
npm install
```

### Environment Configuration

Copy `.env.example` to `.env`:

```bash
cp .env.example .env
```

For local development without Firebase:
```
VITE_DATA_MODE=mock
```

### Run Development Server

```bash
npm run dev
```

### Build for Production

```bash
npm run build
```

### Run Linter

```bash
npm run lint
```

### Run Verification Suites

End-to-end suites live in `scripts/` (Puppeteer, mock mode — they drive the real UI and assert on the DOM and mock-only local state).

| Suite | Covers |
|-------|--------|
| `notification-routing-test.cjs` | Admin → Waiter bell (menu/tables), no waiter → supervisor link, inventory admin ⇄ supervisor |
| `waiter-token-flow-test.cjs` | Cart → KOT → token printed → Admin → Payments → Token History |
| `bill-settlement-test.cjs` | Bill → payment → order auto-completes → LIVE board clears |
| `bill-empty-test.cjs` | Bill cannot be generated on an order-less session |
| `order-lifecycle-test.cjs` | Dine-in + parcel live orders, separate token series, settlement |
| `order-confirm-test.cjs` | Session popup → Menu / Order → confirmed order with token |
| `print-receipt-check.cjs` | Digest previews print only the paper, never the app UI |
| `table-area-grouping-test.cjs` | Area-wise grouping on admin + waiter views |
| `runtime-crud-test.cjs` / `fresh-crud-test.cjs` | Table + inventory CRUD, persistence, reset |
| `runtime-dataflow-test.cjs` | Dashboard stats react to data changes |
| `relay-concurrency-test.cjs` | Print relay concurrency, duplicate protection, routing isolation |

## Mock Mode (DEVELOPMENT/TESTING ONLY)

Mock mode (`VITE_DATA_MODE=mock`) is for local development and automated UI
tests ONLY. It uses in-memory state managed by React Context, allowing full
frontend development without Firebase. **Mock mode must never be used in
production** — nothing would persist.

### Mock Users
- `admin@beeshive.local` - Admin access
- `waiter@beeshive.local` - Waiter access
- `supervisor@beeshive.local` - Supervisor access

## Firebase Mode (PRODUCTION)

**Production runs with `VITE_DATA_MODE=firebase`.** All authoritative
restaurant/business data (users, tables, menu, sessions, orders, tokens,
bills, payments, inventory, purchase requests, notifications, audit logs,
settings, analytics snapshots and the durable `printJobs` history) is
persisted in Firebase Auth + Cloud Firestore + Cloud Storage. Browser
local/session storage is used ONLY for non-business UI preferences (e.g. a
waiter's table-filter choice) and is actively cleaned of mock keys in
Firebase mode.

To enable Firebase (production):

1. Create a Firebase project at https://console.firebase.google.com
2. Enable Authentication (Email/Password)
3. Create a Cloud Firestore database and deploy `firestore.rules`
4. Enable Cloud Storage and deploy `storage.rules`
5. Copy Firebase config values to `.env`:
   ```
   VITE_DATA_MODE=firebase
   VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY=your-api-key
   VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=your-project.firebaseapp.com
   VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=your-project-id
   VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET=your-project.appspot.com
   VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID=your-sender-id
   VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID=your-app-id
   ```
6. Deploy Firestore security rules from `firestore.rules`
7. Deploy Storage security rules from `storage.rules`

## Firestore Collections

| Collection | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `users` | Staff profiles with roles |
| `tables` | Restaurant table configurations |
| `menuCategories` | Menu category definitions |
| `menu` | Individual dish items with images |
| `diningSessions` | Active dining sessions per table |
| `orders` | Orders linked to sessions |
| `bills` | Generated bills |
| `inventory` | Restaurant inventory |
| `purchaseRequests` | Restocking requests |
| `notifications` | Role-based notifications |
| `activityLog` | Audit trail |
| `paymentRecords` | Payment records |
| `settings` | Restaurant configuration |

## Firestore Security Rules

See `firestore.rules` for the complete security configuration:

- **Admin**: Full read/write access to all collections
- **Waiter**: Read tables/menu/sessions/orders, write sessions/orders (billing/payments are admin-only)
- **Supervisor**: Read orders/menu/inventory, write menu availability/images/inventory/purchase requests

## Image Storage

Dish images are stored in Firebase Cloud Storage:
- Path: `restaurants/{restaurantId}/menu/{menuItemId}/original`
- Only `imageUrl` and `imagePath` are stored in Firestore
- Supported formats: JPEG, PNG, WEBP
- Max file size: 5MB

## Staff Account Creation

When Firebase is connected, staff accounts are created directly by the web application using Firebase Authentication + Firestore:

1. Admin fills in staff details in the app (name, username, email, phone, password, role, photo)
2. The app creates a Firebase Authentication account for the staff member
3. The app creates a `users/{uid}` Firestore profile document
4. Username, email, and phone mappings are reserved transactionally for uniqueness
5. Profile image is uploaded to Firebase Storage (Firestore stores only the URL)
6. Returns success to the admin

Username, email, and phone must be unique across ALL users (admins, supervisors, waiters).

**Important**: Never put Firebase Admin SDK credentials in frontend code.

## Architecture

```
src/
├── components/     # Reusable UI components
├── context/        # React Context providers (auth, restaurant state, sidebar)
├── pages/          # Role-based dashboard pages
├── services/
│   ├── firebase/   # Firebase service layer (auth, firestore, storage)
│   └── print/      # Print queue + DIVYE PT-210 print service
└── App.tsx         # Main application with routing
```

## Printing (DIVYE PT-210)

The application supports two DIVYE PT-210 thermal printers:

- **PT-210 #1 (Kitchen)**: Prints tokens, KOTs, and parcel tokens only
- **PT-210 #2 (Admin)**: Prints customer bills, paid receipts, and reprints only

See `docs/pt210-deployment.md` for setup instructions.

### Print Routing Isolation

- Waiter tokens → Kitchen PT-210 #1 only
- Admin bills → Admin PT-210 #2 only
- Bill reprints → Admin PT-210 #2 only (explicit new print job)

The Windows Print Relay (`scripts/print-server.cjs`) handles job routing and concurrency.

## Build Commands

| Command | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `npm run dev` | Start development server |
| `npm run build` | Build for production |
| `npm run lint` | Run ESLint |

## Tech Stack

- **Frontend**: React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- **Routing**: React Router v6
- **Icons**: Lucide React
- **Build**: Vite
- **Backend** (optional): Firebase (Auth, Firestore, Storage, Functions)

import os
from pathlib import Path

# Directories and files to ignore during scanning
IGNORE_DIRS = {
    'node_modules', '.git', 'dist', 'build', '.vite', 
    '__pycache__', '.idea', '.vscode', 'coverage'
}

IGNORE_FILES = {
    'project_structure.txt', 'generate_structure.py', 
    '.DS_Store', 'thumbs.db', 'package-lock.json', 'yarn.lock'
}

OUTPUT_FILE = 'project_structure.txt'

def build_tree(dir_path: Path, prefix: str = '') -> list[str]:
    """Recursively builds tree structure representation as a list of strings."""
    lines = []
    
    # Filter and sort contents (directories first, then files)
    try:
        entries = sorted(
            [e for e in dir_path.iterdir() if e.name not in IGNORE_DIRS and e.name not in IGNORE_FILES],
            key=lambda e: (not e.is_dir(), e.name.lower())
        )
    except PermissionError:
        return lines

    count = len(entries)
    for index, entry in enumerate(entries):
        is_last = (index == count - 1)
        connector = '└── ' if is_last else '├── '
        
        if entry.is_dir():
            lines.append(f"{prefix}{connector}{entry.name}/")
            extension = '    ' if is_last else '│   '
            lines.extend(build_tree(entry, prefix + extension))
        else:
            lines.append(f"{prefix}{connector}{entry.name}")

    return lines

def main():
    root_dir = Path.cwd()
    project_name = root_dir.name

    print(f"Scanning project root: {root_dir}")

    tree_lines = [f"{project_name}/"]
    tree_lines.extend(build_tree(root_dir))

    with open(OUTPUT_FILE, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as f:
        f.write('\n'.join(tree_lines) + '\n')

    print(f"Successfully generated project structure in '{OUTPUT_FILE}'!")

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

# PT-210 Thermal Printer Deployment Guide (Bee's Hive)

This guide is for the **non-technical restaurant operator**. It sets up the two
DIVYE PT-210 58mm thermal printers with the Bee's Hive central print relay on
the Windows computer.

| Printer | Role | Transport | Prints |
|---|---|---|---|
| PT-210 **#1** | KITCHEN | Bluetooth (production target) — or USB | Tokens / KOT / parcel tokens only |
| PT-210 **#2** | ADMIN | USB (USB-A → USB-C) | Customer bills / paid receipts only |

Production hybrid target: **Kitchen PT-210 over Bluetooth + Admin PT-210 over
USB, both on the SAME Windows laptop** — see **§13**. The classic two-USB
setup (§1–§12) keeps working unchanged.

The Windows computer is the **central print relay**. Waiter phones never talk
to a printer directly — they send jobs over Wi-Fi to this computer, which
prints them one-by-one in order. Waiter phones **never** pair with the
Kitchen Bluetooth printer; the laptop owns the single connection.

---

## 1. Windows requirements

- Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit).
- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) LTS installed (comes with the Bee's Hive app package).
- Two free USB ports (or a powered USB hub).
- Printer and waiter phones on the **same Wi-Fi network**.

## 2. Connect the PT-210 printers

1. Load 58mm thermal paper into both printers (paper rolls **out from the top**).
2. Connect PT-210 **#2** (admin) to a USB port with the USB-A → USB-C cable.
   For the Kitchen printer either connect PT-210 **#1** to a different USB
   port (classic setup) **or** pair it with the laptop over Bluetooth
   (production hybrid target — full steps in **§13**). Note which physical
   printer is which.
3. Power both printers ON. The power LED should be solid.

## 3. Driver installation

1. Plug in the first PT-210 → Windows shows *"Setting up a device…"*.
2. If the PT-210 came with a driver CD/USB, run the installer. Most PT-210
   units are detected by Windows as a generic **58mm/POS-80/ESC-POS thermal
   printer** with no extra driver.
3. Repeat for the second printer.

## 4. Identify each PT-210 in Windows

1. Press **Start**, type **Printers & scanners**, open it.
2. You should see two new printer entries, e.g.
   `58mm Thermal Printer` / `58mm Thermal Printer (Copy 1)` or `POS-58`.
3. **Do a physical check:** click each entry → **Printing preferences** →
   **Print Test Page** — the paper comes out of the printer you are checking.
4. Note the exact name of the entry that belongs to the KITCHEN printer and
   the exact name for the ADMIN printer.

## 5. Rename the Windows printer queues (recommended)

Clear names prevent mix-ups:

1. In **Printers & scanners**, click the kitchen printer → **Remove** is NOT
   needed — instead click **Manage** → **Printer properties**.
2. On the **General** tab change the name to:

   ```
   BeeShive Kitchen PT210
   ```

3. Repeat for the admin printer → `BeeShive Admin PT210`.
4. Renaming requires administrator rights if prompted.

> The relay does **not** require these exact names — any Windows printer name
> works as long as it matches the environment variables in step 6.

## 6. Environment variables

Create the file `.env.print-relay` **in the beeshive folder** (next to
`package.json`) with these lines (adjust names to step 4/5):

```
PRINT_PORT=8787
BIND_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0
KITCHEN_PRINTER_NAME=BeeShive Kitchen PT210
ADMIN_PRINTER_NAME=BeeShive Admin PT210
PRINT_RETRY_ATTEMPTS=3
CORS_ORIGIN=*
```

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `PRINT_PORT` | Relay web port (use the same number everywhere). |
| `BIND_ADDRESS` | `0.0.0.0` = accept jobs from waiter phones on the LAN. |
| `KITCHEN_PRINTER_NAME` | Exact Windows name of the kitchen PT-210. |
| `ADMIN_PRINTER_NAME` | Exact Windows name of the admin PT-210. |
| `PRINT_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` | Total physical attempts per job before it is FAILED (default 3; the Admin app sends its Print Retry Count setting, range 1–10). |
| `SPOOL_DRAIN_SECONDS` | After writing bytes, wait up to N seconds for the print job to leave the spool queue (proof it reached the printer). Default 20, `0` disables. |
| `API_KEY` | Optional shared secret; if set, callers must send header `X-Api-Key`. |
| `CORS_ORIGIN` | Browser origin allowed to submit jobs (`*` for a closed LAN). |

> **Hybrid Bluetooth setup** (Kitchen PT-210 over Bluetooth, Admin over USB)
> adds `KITCHEN_PRINTER_TRANSPORT`, `KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_PORT` and
> `KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_BAUD` — see **§13**. Existing USB-only values keep
> working unchanged; nothing here needs to be removed.

## 7. Start the relay (normal daily use)

Double-click **`start-print-relay.cmd`** (in the beeshive folder). A black
window opens showing:

```
Bee's Hive print relay on http://0.0.0.0:8787
kitchen printer (windows-spooler): BeeShive Kitchen PT210
admin printer (windows-spooler): BeeShive Admin PT210
```

Leave this window open while the restaurant is open. In the Bee's Hive admin
settings, set:

- Kitchen relay URL → `http://<this-computer-ip>:8787`
- Admin relay URL → `http://<this-computer-ip>:8787`

(Find the computer IP with `ipconfig` — e.g. `192.168.1.20`.)

## 8. Test the kitchen printer

Open a browser on the Windows computer and, with the relay window open, run in
a new terminal:

```
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/kitchen
```

**Paper must come out of PT-210 #1** with:

```
==== KITCHEN PRINTER TEST ====
PT-210 #1 (KITCHEN) ...
```

If nothing prints or the error says *printer not found*, re-check step 4-6
(exact name match, USB cable, power).

## 9. Test the admin printer

```
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/admin
```

**Paper must come out of PT-210 #2** with `==== ADMIN PRINTER TEST ====`.
Nothing may print on the kitchen printer.

## 10. Diagnosing a printer that looks offline

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| Relay says `printer not found: …` | Printer name in env file ≠ Windows name (step 4). USB cable unplugged. Printer powered off. |
| Job shows `spooler write failed` | Paper out / cover open — load paper, close cover, then press **Retry Print** in the app. |
| Jobs stuck at `PRINTING` | Close the relay window, unplug-replug the printer USB, start the relay again. |
| Waiter phones say *relay unavailable* | Relay window closed or computer asleep — restart the relay (step 11), check Wi-Fi. |
| Windows Print Queue shows stuck jobs | Open **Printers & scanners** → printer → **Open print queue** → right-click each job → **Cancel**, then retry. |
| Test page prints garbage or blank | The installed driver is a GDI/render driver, not ESC-POS raw. Install the vendor PT-210 driver in ESC/POS mode, or add the printer again on the same USB port with the **Generic / Text Only** driver and point `*_PRINTER_NAME` at that queue. |

Check relay health any time: open `http://127.0.0.1:8787/printers` in a browser
on the relay computer. `available: true` = printer visible to Windows.

## 11. Restart the relay after a Windows reboot

The relay does **not** auto-start. After every reboot:

1. Double-click **`start-print-relay.cmd`**.
2. Confirm both printer lines show your Windows printer names (not
   "NOT CONFIGURED").
3. Send one test print per printer (steps 8-9).

To make this automatic, press **Start**, type **Task Scheduler**, create a
basic task: trigger *At log on*, action *Start a program*:

```
Program:  cmd.exe
Arguments: /c start-print-relay.cmd
Start in:  <the beeshive folder path>
```

## 12. Operator quick reference

- **Token not printed?** → kitchen printer paper/Bluetooth → press **Retry Print**.
  (Bluetooth kitchen: printer ON, laptop Bluetooth ON, in range —
  `http://127.0.0.1:8787/printers` must show Kitchen `available: true`.)
- **Bill not printed?** → admin printer paper/USB → press **Retry Print**.
- **Need an extra copy?** → use **Reprint** (this intentionally prints again).
- Never point the kitchen relay URL at the admin computer or vice versa.
- Never swap the two printers to "make it work" — a Kitchen failure is
  reported honestly; fix the Kitchen link (**§13.5**), never reroute bills
  to the Admin printer (the relay never silently redirects).

## 13. Hybrid setup — Kitchen PT-210 over Bluetooth + Admin PT-210 over USB

Target physical layout — **ONE** Windows laptop is the print server for BOTH
printers:

```
                SAME WINDOWS LAPTOP
             ┌────────────────────────────┐
             │  BeeShive Print Relay      │
             │  Kitchen → Bluetooth       │
             │  Admin   → USB             │
             └──────────┬─────────────────┘
                        │
          ┌─────────────┴─────────────┐
       Bluetooth                      USB
          │                            │
          ▼                            ▼
   PT-210 #1 KITCHEN            PT-210 #2 ADMIN/BILL
```

5+ waiter phones → Wi-Fi → that same laptop. Waiter phones **never** pair
with the Kitchen printer; the laptop owns the single Bluetooth connection
and the relay serializes every Kitchen job through one queue, so concurrent
waiters can never interleave thermal output or fight over the link.

### 13.1 The two real Windows Bluetooth paths (use the one Windows gives you)

**Path A — Windows exposes the paired PT-210 as a normal printer queue.**
Pair the PT-210, confirm the queue appears in *Printers & scanners*, keep
`KITCHEN_PRINTER_NAME`. The relay writes raw ESC/POS through the Windows
spooler exactly as the USB setup does (transport stays `windows-spooler`) —
Windows itself rides that queue over Bluetooth. Nothing else changes.

**Path B — Windows exposes the PT-210 only as a Bluetooth COM port**
(Serial Port Profile; Device Manager → Ports (COM & LPT) → *Standard Serial
over Bluetooth link (COMx)*). Set in `.env.print-relay`:

```
KITCHEN_PRINTER_TRANSPORT=bluetooth
KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_PORT=COM5
```

The relay opens that COM port with .NET `System.IO.Ports.SerialPort`
(PowerShell helper) and writes the **same** raw ESC/POS bytes — same 58mm
token/KOT/parcel/bill formatting, no changes to receipt content. Transport
shows as `bluetooth`. There is no browser printing, no simulation, no mock
and no fallback to the Admin printer: if the Bluetooth PT-210 cannot be
reached, the Kitchen job fails with a real error and the SAME job (token
number already persisted in Firebase) can be retried.

The Admin PT-210 keeps its USB-A → USB-C connection and the existing
`ADMIN_PRINTER_NAME` windows-spooler path — completely unchanged.

### 13.2 One-time pairing of the Kitchen PT-210

1. Windows → **Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Add device → Bluetooth** →
   select the PT-210 → pair (PIN `0000` or `1234` if asked).
2. Check **Device Manager → Ports (COM & LPT)** for *Standard Serial over
   Bluetooth link (COMx)* (or the device → Properties → COM Port) and note
   the COM number.
   - If instead Windows created a **printer queue** (Printers & scanners),
     use Path A (§13.1) — skip step 3 and keep `KITCHEN_PRINTER_NAME`.
3. In `.env.print-relay` add (leave the Admin lines unchanged):

   ```
   KITCHEN_PRINTER_TRANSPORT=bluetooth
   KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_PORT=COM5
   ```

4. Restart **start-print-relay.cmd**. The console must show:

   ```
   Bee's Hive print relay on http://0.0.0.0:8787
   kitchen printer (bluetooth): COM5
   admin printer (windows-spooler): BeeShive Admin PT210
   ```

5. Health check — open `http://127.0.0.1:8787/printers`:

   ```
   kitchen: {"configured": true, "transport": "bluetooth", "available": true, ...}
   admin:   {"configured": true, "transport": "windows-spooler", "available": true, ...}
   ```

   `available: false` on Kitchen means Windows cannot reach the Bluetooth
   printer right now (not paired / powered off / laptop Bluetooth off /
   out of range / port busy) — the `error` field says which. The relay
   NEVER reports `available: true` just because it is running: it probes
   the real COM port (present + device status + openable), cached 10 s.

### 13.3 New environment variables (additive — old installs unaffected)

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `KITCHEN_PRINTER_TRANSPORT` | Optional override: `bluetooth` / `windows-spooler` / `tcp`. Unset = auto: `KITCHEN_PRINTER_NAME` wins (original behaviour), else Bluetooth if only `KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_PORT` is set, else legacy TCP. |
| `KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_PORT` | Paired Bluetooth SPP COM port of the Kitchen PT-210 (e.g. `COM5`). |
| `KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_BAUD` | Optional serial baud (default `9600`). |
| `ADMIN_PRINTER_TRANSPORT` | Same override for Admin (Bluetooth supported if ever needed; production target keeps Admin on USB). |
| `ADMIN_BLUETOOTH_PORT` / `ADMIN_BLUETOOTH_BAUD` | Same, for an Admin Bluetooth printer. |

Existing `KITCHEN_PRINTER_NAME` / `ADMIN_PRINTER_NAME` keep working exactly as
before: a **Kitchen USB + Admin USB** installation is unaffected. No old
variable was removed.

### 13.4 Failure behaviour (honest failures — never faked)

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Laptop Bluetooth off / printer off / out of range / unpaired | Kitchen job → `FAILED` with a Bluetooth-specific reason (`Kitchen Bluetooth (COM5): …`). Visible on the app's **Retry Print** error, at `http://127.0.0.1:8787/jobs`, and in the Firestore `printJobs` record. |
| Retry | The SAME job id is retried (`PRINT_RETRY_ATTEMPTS`). A retry never creates a second token — the printed token always uses the already-persisted `order.tokenNumber`. |
| Kitchen Bluetooth down, Admin USB fine | Only Kitchen jobs fail; Admin bills keep printing (independent queues, independent transports). |
| Admin USB down, Kitchen Bluetooth fine | Only Admin jobs fail, with a spooler-specific error (never mentions Bluetooth). |
| Never happens | Kitchen token silently printed on the Admin printer; browser-print fallback; fake `PRINTED`; payment marked successful because a receipt printed. |

Billing, payments, GST, bill numbers, token sequencing and Firebase
persistence are untouched by this transport change — the relay only receives
already-formatted 58mm lines and writes them to the configured physical
transport. Firebase remains the production source of truth; the Bluetooth
COM connection is operational runtime state only, never a business database.

### 13.5 Bluetooth troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `Bluetooth printer not connected: port COMx is not present` | Re-pair the PT-210, keep laptop Bluetooth ON, and make `KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_PORT` match Device Manager. |
| `reports status … (powered off, out of range, or laptop Bluetooth disabled)` | Power the printer on / move it closer, then press **Retry Print**. |
| `/printers` kitchen shows `available: false` | The `error` field names the cause — fix it and re-check (results refresh every 10 s). |
| Prints once, then fails | Another app opened the COM port (vendor utility, second relay instance) — close it. |
| Windows reassigned the COM port after re-pairing | Update `KITCHEN_BLUETOOTH_PORT` and restart the relay. |
| Kitchen jobs fail but `/test/admin` works | Expected: transports are independent — fix the Kitchen Bluetooth link (§13.2); never repoint Kitchen at the Admin printer. |

The full physical acceptance procedure (both printers, FIFO, disconnect /
reconnect, multi-waiter) is **Appendix C** — Bluetooth must not be signed
off until it passes on real hardware.

## Appendix B — DEPLOYMENT-DAY HARDWARE TEST PROCEDURE (mandatory)

The software side is fully verified in mock mode and against the Windows
spooler error paths. The ONLY unverified link is the physical PT-210
hardware. Perform this on deployment day, in order, and do not open the
restaurant until every check passes.

**Setup (one-time, ~15 minutes)**

1. Connect PT-210 #1 (kitchen) and PT-210 #2 (admin) by USB, power both on,
   load 58mm thermal paper (roll feeds from the top).
2. `Start → Printers & scanners` — confirm two new printer entries appear.
3. Identify which entry is which: click each printer → `Print Test Page` →
   note which physical printer produced the page.
4. Rename the queues: `BeeShive Kitchen PT210` and `BeeShive Admin PT210`
   (printer properties → General tab).
5. Create `.env.print-relay` in the beeshive folder:
   ```
   PRINT_PORT=8787
   KITCHEN_PRINTER_NAME=BeeShive Kitchen PT210
   ADMIN_PRINTER_NAME=BeeShive Admin PT210
   ```
6. Start `start-print-relay.cmd` — both lines must show the printer names in
   parentheses as `windows-spooler` (never `NOT CONFIGURED`).
7. Health check — in a browser on the relay PC open:
   `http://127.0.0.1:8787/printers`
   → both roles must show `"configured": true, "available": true, "transport": "windows-spooler"`.

**Check 1 — kitchen physical print (PT-210 #1)**

```
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/kitchen
```
→ Paper MUST come out of PT-210 #1 with `==== KITCHEN PRINTER TEST ====`.
→ PT-210 #2 must print NOTHING.
→ If garbage/blank: fix the driver (see §10) and repeat.
→ If FAILED: `curl.exe http://127.0.0.1:8787/jobs` shows the exact reason.

**Check 2 — admin physical print (PT-210 #2)**

```
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/admin
```
→ Paper MUST come out of PT-210 #2 only.

**Check 3 — FIFO serialization under load (kitchen)**

Run three rapid kitchen jobs from three different waiter phones (or repeat
the curl command three times quickly):
```
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/kitchen
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/kitchen
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/kitchen
```
→ PT-210 #1 must print three receipts, top to bottom, strictly in submit
order (compare the RELAY TIME line on each). One at a time, never interleaved.

**Check 4 — routing isolation**

Create one real order from a waiter phone AND one real bill from Admin.
→ The token prints on PT-210 #1 only; the bill prints on PT-210 #2 only.

**Check 5 — duplicate protection**

```
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/print -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"id\":\"dupe_check_1\",\"kind\":\"token\",\"printer\":\"kitchen\",\"lines\":[\"DUPLICATE CHECK\"]}"
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/print -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d "{\"id\":\"dupe_check_1\",\"kind\":\"token\",\"printer\":\"kitchen\",\"lines\":[\"DUPLICATE CHECK\"]}"
```
→ The FIRST call queues and prints one receipt. The SECOND call (same job id)
must respond `"duplicate": true` and NO second receipt may come out.
Then use the app's **Reprint** button on a printed bill — exactly one extra
receipt MUST print (an explicit reprint is an intentional new job).

**Check 6 — disconnect failure (honest failure semantics)**

With Check 1 passing, unplug PT-210 #1's USB cable, then run the kitchen
test curl again.
→ The job must report FAILED (status visible at `http://127.0.0.1:8787/jobs`)
with a printer-offline/not-found reason — never PRINTED.
→ Reconnect the USB, wait 5 seconds, retry — it must print again.
Note: some drivers keep accepting spool jobs even when the device is gone.
The relay's post-write drain check (`SPOOL_DRAIN_SECONDS`, default 20) detects
this for any driver that exposes spool jobs. If the real PT-210 driver still
reports PRINTED while disconnected, switch that queue to the
**Generic / Text Only** driver (same USB port) — it exposes jobs, letting the
drain check catch the disconnect — and record the result here.

**Check 7 — end-of-test state**

```
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/kitchen
curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/admin
```
→ Both printers produce their test receipts one final time. Restaurant may open.

---

## Appendix C — HYBRID USB + BLUETOOTH PHYSICAL TEST (mandatory before sign-off)

Software/build/TypeScript tests alone do **NOT** prove Bluetooth works. Run
this on the deployment laptop with both real PT-210s. **Do not mark
Bluetooth verification complete until every step passes on hardware.**

1. Pair Kitchen PT-210 with the Windows laptop (§13.2 steps 1–2).
2. Verify Windows recognises the Bluetooth connection (Device Manager COM
   port exists, or a Windows printer queue exists — Path A).
3. Start the relay → `http://127.0.0.1:8787/printers` shows Kitchen
   `transport: "bluetooth"` (`"windows-spooler"` on Path A) and
   `available: true`.
4. Connect Admin PT-210 to the SAME laptop using USB-A → USB-C; power on.
5. Verify `/printers` shows BOTH roles `configured: true, available: true`
   with their own transports (Kitchen bluetooth / Admin windows-spooler).
6. `curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/kitchen`
   → ONLY PT-210 #1 prints; the slip's `TRANSPORT` line shows the real path.
7. `curl.exe -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8787/test/admin`
   → ONLY PT-210 #2 prints; PT-210 #1 prints NOTHING.
8. Send 3+ Kitchen jobs rapidly (three test curls back-to-back).
   → They print strictly in submit order, one at a time, never interleaved.
9. Send Kitchen and Admin jobs close together.
   → Each reaches the correct physical printer (routing isolation).
10. Real order from a waiter phone + real bill from Admin → token only on
    PT-210 #1, bill only on PT-210 #2.
11. Disable laptop Bluetooth (or power off the Kitchen printer).
12. Send a Kitchen job → it must report FAILED/retryable with a Bluetooth
    reason at `http://127.0.0.1:8787/jobs` — never PRINTED, never on the
    Admin printer, never a browser print dialog.
13. Re-enable Bluetooth / power the printer back on.
14. Retry the SAME job from the app → it prints; the token number is
    IDENTICAL (no second token — Firestore `printJobs` shows one job id).
15. Kill and restart the relay → both transports recover; `/printers`
    healthy again; no duplicate jobs replayed.
16. Restart Windows → start the relay → repeat checks 6 and 7.
17. Run the automated suites:
    ```
    node scripts/relay-transport-test.cjs      (hybrid transport honesty)
    node scripts/relay-concurrency-test.cjs    (FIFO/duplicates, PRINT_MOCK=1 relay)
    ```
18. Multi-waiter load: 5 phones place orders rapidly → all Kitchen tokens
    print in order, none lost, none interleaved; Admin bills unaffected.
19. Paper-out / cover-open on Kitchen → FAILED with a real reason; **Retry
    Print** after reloading paper reprints the SAME token.
20. Record results here: ______________ (date / initials)

Physical Bluetooth verification status: **NOT YET PERFORMED** — must be
completed on the deployment laptop with the real PT-210 hardware before the
hybrid setup is considered done.

        throw new functions.https.HttpsError('invalid-argument', 'uid and a strong password are required.');

    const targetDoc = await admin.firestore().collection('users').doc(uid).get();
    const target = targetDoc.data();
    if ((target === null || target === void 0 ? void 0 : target.isMainAdmin) === true && caller.isMainAdmin !== true) {
        throw new functions.https.HttpsError('permission-denied', 'Only the Main Admin can change that password.');
    }
    await admin.auth().updateUser(uid, { password });
    return { ok: true };
});

import * as functions from 'firebase-functions'
import * as admin from 'firebase-admin'

if (!admin.apps.length) {
  admin.initializeApp()
}

/**
 * Admin-only: set Firebase Auth password for any uid.
 * Called from the web app when an admin edits a staff password.
 */
export const adminSetPassword = functions.https.onCall(async (data, context) => {
  if (!context.auth) {
    throw new functions.https.HttpsError('unauthenticated', 'Sign in required.')
  }

  const callerUid = context.auth.uid
  const callerDoc = await admin.firestore().collection('users').doc(callerUid).get()
  const caller = callerDoc.data()

  if (!caller || caller.role !== 'admin' || caller.active === false) {
    throw new functions.https.HttpsError('permission-denied', 'Admin only.')
  }

  const uid = String(data?.uid ?? '').trim()
  const password = String(data?.password ?? '')

  if (!uid || password.length < 8) {
    throw new functions.https.HttpsError(
      'invalid-argument',
      'uid and a strong password are required.',
    )
  }

  const targetDoc = await admin.firestore().collection('users').doc(uid).get()
  const target = targetDoc.data()

  if (target?.isMainAdmin === true && caller.isMainAdmin !== true) {
    throw new functions.https.HttpsError(
      'permission-denied',
      'Only the Main Admin can change that password.',
    )
  }

  await admin.auth().updateUser(uid, { password })
  return { ok: true }
})

import { lazy, Suspense } from 'react'
import { BrowserRouter, Routes, Route, Navigate } from 'react-router-dom'
import { dataMode, isFirebaseConfigured } from './services/firebase/config'
import { AuthProvider, useAuth } from './context/AuthContext'
import { RestaurantProvider } from './context/RestaurantContext'
import { SidebarProvider } from './context/SidebarContext'
import ProtectedRoute from './components/ProtectedRoute'
import Header from './components/Header'
import NotificationToasts from './components/NotificationToasts'
import ErrorBoundary from './components/ErrorBoundary'
import Login from './pages/Login'

// Role dashboards are code-split: the waiter floor only downloads the waiter
// bundle, the counter admin only the admin bundle — faster first paint on the
// phone that is already walking to the table.
const AdminDashboard = lazy(() => import('./pages/AdminDashboard'))
const WaiterDashboard = lazy(() => import('./pages/WaiterDashboard'))
const SupervisorDashboard = lazy(() => import('./pages/SupervisorDashboard'))
const NotificationsHistory = lazy(() => import('./pages/NotificationsHistory'))

function LoadingScreen({ label = 'Loading…' }: { label?: string }) {
  return (
    <div className="flex min-h-[60vh] items-center justify-center px-4">
      <div className="text-center">
        <div className="mx-auto mb-4 h-10 w-10 animate-spin rounded-full border-4 border-orange-500 border-t-transparent"></div>
        <p className="text-slate-600">{label}</p>
      </div>
    </div>
  )
}

function AppLayout() {
  const { user, isAuthenticated, isLoading } = useAuth()

  if (isLoading) {
    return (
      <div className="flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center bg-linear-to-br from-orange-50 to-amber-50">
        <div className="text-center">
          <div className="mx-auto mb-4 h-10 w-10 animate-spin rounded-full border-4 border-orange-500 border-t-transparent"></div>
          <p className="text-slate-600">Loading...</p>
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }

  if (!isAuthenticated || !user) {
    return (
      <Routes>
        <Route path="/login" element={<Login />} />
        <Route path="*" element={<Navigate to="/login" replace />} />
      </Routes>
    )
  }

  return (
    <div className="min-h-screen bg-linear-to-b from-[#fff9f0] via-[#fff4ea] to-[#ffefdf] text-slate-800">
      <Header />
      <NotificationToasts />

      <main className="min-w-0 max-w-full px-3 py-4 sm:px-4 sm:py-6 md:px-6 lg:px-8">
        {/* Top-level guard: a crash anywhere in a dashboard shows a recoverable
            panel instead of a blank page (issue: menus going blank). */}
        <ErrorBoundary label={`${user.role} panel`} resetKey={user.role}>
          <Suspense fallback={<LoadingScreen />}>
            <Routes>
            {/* Home - Show appropriate view based on role */}
            <Route
              path="/"
              element={
                user.role === 'admin' ? (
                  <Navigate to="/admin" replace />
                ) : user.role === 'waiter' ? (
                  <Navigate to="/waiter" replace />
                ) : user.role === 'supervisor' ? (
                  <Navigate to="/supervisor" replace />
                ) : (
                  <Navigate to="/login" replace />
                )
              }
            />

            <Route path="/login" element={<Navigate to="/" replace />} />

            {/* Admin Dashboard */}
            <Route
              path="/admin"
              element={
                <ProtectedRoute requiredRole="admin">
                  <AdminDashboard />
                </ProtectedRoute>
              }
            />

            {/* Waiter Dashboard */}
            <Route
              path="/waiter"
              element={
                <ProtectedRoute requiredRole="waiter">
                  <WaiterDashboard />
                </ProtectedRoute>
              }
            />

            {/* Supervisor Dashboard */}
            <Route
              path="/supervisor"
              element={
                <ProtectedRoute requiredRole="supervisor">
                  <SupervisorDashboard />
                </ProtectedRoute>
              }
            />

            {/* Notification History (all roles) */}
            <Route
              path="/notifications"
              element={
                <ProtectedRoute>
                  <NotificationsHistory />
                </ProtectedRoute>
              }
            />
          </Routes>
          </Suspense>
        </ErrorBoundary>
      </main>
    </div>
  )
}

function App() {
  if (dataMode === 'firebase' && !isFirebaseConfigured()) {
    return (
      <div className="flex min-h-screen items-center justify-center bg-slate-50 p-6">
        <div className="max-w-lg rounded-2xl border border-red-200 bg-white p-6 shadow-sm">
          <h1 className="text-xl font-bold text-red-700">Firebase configuration required</h1>
          <p className="mt-2 text-sm text-slate-600">
            Firebase production storage is not configured. The application is stopped so business data cannot be kept only in temporary browser memory.
          </p>
        </div>
      </div>
    )
  }
  return (
    <BrowserRouter>
      <AuthProvider>
        <RestaurantProvider>
          <SidebarProvider>
            <AppLayout />
          </SidebarProvider>
        </RestaurantProvider>
      </AuthProvider>
    </BrowserRouter>
  )
}

export default App

// Firebase SDK handles (backwards-compatible re-exports).
//
// The single authoritative configuration — and the ONLY `initializeApp` call
// site — lives in services/firebase/config.ts, which initializes the Firebase
// App plus Authentication, Cloud Firestore and Cloud Storage from it. This
// module merely re-exports those handles, so every historical import path
// ('../firebase') keeps working without creating a second Firebase app or
// pointing any feature at a different project.
export {
  getAppNow,
  getAuthNow,
  getFirestoreNow,
  getStorageNow,
  getFirebaseServices,
  firebaseProjectId,
} from './services/firebase/config'

import { useCallback, useEffect, useState } from 'react'
import { useAuth, MAX_ADMINS } from '../context/AuthContext'
import Avatar from './Avatar'
import AvatarUpload from './AvatarUpload'
import { uploadMemberImage, deleteMemberImage, getMemberImagePath } from '../services/firebase/storageService'
import { isValidContactEmailFormat, isValidPhone } from '../services/firebase/userService'
import { validateUsername } from '../lib/username'
import { validatePassword } from '../lib/password'
import { Plus, Trash2, Crown, UserCog, X, Shield, CheckCircle, Mail, Phone, Calendar, BadgeCheck, CheckCircle2, Circle, AlertCircle } from 'lucide-react'

type Admin = ReturnType<typeof useAuth>['listAdmins'] extends () => (infer T)[] ? T : never

/**
 * The password policy is defined ONCE in `lib/password.ts`; the checklist below
 * is rendered from the same rule list that is enforced before a save, so the
 * guidance and the enforcement can never drift apart.
 */
const PASSWORD_RULES: string[] = validatePassword('').errors

const PasswordChecklist = ({ password, confirm }: { password: string; confirm: string }) => {
  if (password.length === 0 && confirm.length === 0) return null
  const failures = validatePassword(password).errors
  const mismatch = confirm.length > 0 && confirm !== password
  return (
    <div className="mt-2">
      <ul className="space-y-1">
        {PASSWORD_RULES.map((label) => {
          const ok = !failures.includes(label)
          return (
            <li
              key={label}
              className={`flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs font-medium ${ok ? 'text-emerald-600' : 'text-red-500'}`}
            >
              {ok ? <CheckCircle2 size={12} /> : <Circle size={12} />}
              {label}
            </li>
          )
        })}
      </ul>
      {mismatch && (
        <p className="mt-1.5 flex items-center gap-1.5 text-xs font-semibold text-red-600">
          <AlertCircle size={12} /> Passwords do not match
        </p>
      )}
    </div>
  )
}

export default function AdminAdminManagement() {
  const { user, isMainAdmin, listAdmins, createAdmin, deleteAdmin, transferMainAdmin, updateMyCredentials } = useAuth()
  const [admins, setAdmins] = useState<Admin[]>([])
  const [error, setError] = useState('')
  const [success, setSuccess] = useState('')
  const [showCreate, setShowCreate] = useState(false)
  const [showTransfer, setShowTransfer] = useState<string | null>(null)
  const [form, setForm] = useState({ name: '', username: '', email: '', phone: '', password: '', confirmPassword: '', avatarUrl: '' })
  const [formAvatarFile, setFormAvatarFile] = useState<File | null>(null)
  const [myForm, setMyForm] = useState({ name: '', username: '', email: '', phone: '', password: '', confirmPassword: '', currentPassword: '', avatarUrl: '' })
  const [myAvatarFile, setMyAvatarFile] = useState<File | null>(null)
  const [myAvatarChanged, setMyAvatarChanged] = useState(false)
  const [detailsAdmin, setDetailsAdmin] = useState<Admin | null>(null)

const [creating, setCreating] = useState(false)
const [created, setCreated] = useState(false)

const [savingCredentials, setSavingCredentials] = useState(false)
const [credentialsSaved, setCredentialsSaved] = useState(false)

const [deleteCandidate, setDeleteCandidate] = useState<Admin | null>(null)
const [deleting, setDeleting] = useState(false)

  const refresh = useCallback(() => setAdmins(listAdmins()), [listAdmins])
  useEffect(() => { refresh() }, [refresh])

  useEffect(() => {
    if (user && !myAvatarChanged) {
      setMyForm({ name: user.name, username: user.username, email: user.email, phone: user.phone, password: '', confirmPassword: '', currentPassword: '', avatarUrl: user.avatarUrl ?? '' })
    }
  }, [user, myAvatarChanged])

  const adminsFull = admins.length >= MAX_ADMINS

  const handleCreate = async () => {
    setError(''); setSuccess(''); setCreated(false)
    if (!form.name || !form.username || !form.email || !form.phone || !form.password) {
      setError('Name, username, email, phone number and password are all required'); return
    }
    const usernameError = validateUsername(form.username)
    if (usernameError) { setError(usernameError); return }
    if (!isValidContactEmailFormat(form.email)) { setError('Enter a valid email address.'); return }
    if (!isValidPhone(form.phone)) { setError('Phone number must be exactly 10 digits (digits only — no +91, no spaces).'); return }
    const passwordCheck = validatePassword(form.password)
    if (!passwordCheck.isValid) {
      setError(`Password is not strong enough: ${passwordCheck.errors.join('; ')}.`)
      return
    }
    if (form.confirmPassword !== form.password) {
      setError('Password and Confirm Password do not match.')
      return
    }
    setCreating(true)
    setSuccess('Admin account created.')
refresh()

window.setTimeout(() => {
  setCreated(false)
  setShowCreate(false)
}, 1000)
    try {
      const adminData = {
        name: form.name.trim(), username: form.username.trim(), email: form.email.trim(), phone: form.phone.trim(),
        password: form.password, avatarUrl: formAvatarFile ? undefined : form.avatarUrl,
      }
      await createAdmin({ ...adminData, avatarFile: formAvatarFile ?? undefined, isMainAdmin: false, active: true })
      setForm({ name: '', username: '', email: '', phone: '', password: '', confirmPassword: '', avatarUrl: '' })
      setFormAvatarFile(null)
      // The form closes ONLY after the Auth account, Storage image and
      // Firestore profile have all persisted successfully.
      setShowCreate(false)
      setSuccess('Admin account created.')
      refresh()
    } catch (err) {
      // Failure: the form stays open with the real error so it can be corrected.
      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to create admin')
    } finally {
      setCreating(false)
    }
  }

  const handleDelete = (adminId: string) => {
  const admin = admins.find((entry) => entry.id === adminId)

  if (!admin) return

  setDeleteCandidate(admin)
  setError('')
  setSuccess('')
}

const confirmDelete = async () => {
  if (!deleteCandidate || deleting) return

  setDeleting(true)
  setError('')
  setSuccess('')

  try {
    const name = deleteCandidate.name

    await deleteAdmin(deleteCandidate.id)

    setDeleteCandidate(null)
    setSuccess(`Admin "${name}" deleted.`)
    refresh()
  } catch (err) {
    setError(
      err instanceof Error
        ? err.message
        : 'Failed to delete admin'
    )
  } finally {
    setDeleting(false)
  }
}

  const handleTransfer = async (targetId: string, targetName: string) => {
    if (!window.confirm(`Transfer "Main Admin" title to "${targetName}"? You will become a regular Admin.`)) return
    setError(''); setSuccess('')
    try {
      await transferMainAdmin(targetId)
      setShowTransfer(null)
      setSuccess(`Main Admin title transferred to ${targetName}.`)
      refresh()
    } catch (err) {
      setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to transfer title')
    }
  }

  const handleUpdateMe = async () => {
  if (savingCredentials) return

  setError('')
  setSuccess('')
  setCredentialsSaved(false)

  if (!user) return

  const updates: {
    name?: string
    username?: string
    email?: string
    phone?: string
    password?: string
    currentPassword?: string
    avatarUrl?: string
  } = {}

  if (myForm.name.trim() !== user.name) {
    updates.name = myForm.name
  }

  if (
    myForm.username.trim().toLowerCase() !==
    (user.username ?? '')
  ) {
    updates.username = myForm.username
  }

  if (
    myForm.email.trim().toLowerCase() !==
    (user.email ?? '').toLowerCase()
  ) {
    updates.email = myForm.email
  }

  if (myForm.phone.trim() !== (user.phone ?? '')) {
    updates.phone = myForm.phone
  }

  // Username validation
  if (updates.username !== undefined) {
    const usernameError = validateUsername(updates.username)

    if (usernameError) {
      setError(usernameError)
      return
    }

    const normalized = updates.username.trim().toLowerCase()

    if (
      admins.some(
        (entry) =>
          entry.id !== user.id &&
          (entry.username ?? '').toLowerCase() === normalized
      )
    ) {
      setError('That username is already taken.')
      return
    }
  }

  // Email validation
  if (
    updates.email !== undefined &&
    !isValidContactEmailFormat(updates.email)
  ) {
    setError('Enter a valid email address.')
    return
  }

  if (
    updates.email !== undefined &&
    admins.some(
      (entry) =>
        entry.id !== user.id &&
        (entry.email ?? '').toLowerCase() ===
          updates.email!.trim().toLowerCase()
    )
  ) {
    setError('That email address is already in use.')
    return
  }

  // Phone validation
  if (updates.phone !== undefined) {
    if (!isValidPhone(updates.phone)) {
      setError(
        'Phone number must be exactly 10 digits (digits only — no +91, no spaces).'
      )
      return
    }

    if (
      admins.some(
        (entry) =>
          entry.id !== user.id &&
          entry.phone === updates.phone
      )
    ) {
      setError('That phone number is already in use.')
      return
    }
  }

  // Password validation
  if (myForm.password) {
    const passwordCheck = validatePassword(myForm.password)

    if (!passwordCheck.isValid) {
      setError(
        `New password is not strong enough: ${passwordCheck.errors.join('; ')}.`
      )
      return
    }

    if (myForm.confirmPassword !== myForm.password) {
      setError('Password and Confirm Password do not match.')
      return
    }

    if (!myForm.currentPassword) {
      setError('Enter your current password to change it.')
      return
    }

    updates.password = myForm.password
    updates.currentPassword = myForm.currentPassword
  }

  setSavingCredentials(true)

  try {
    let photoRemovedFromStorage = false

    // Profile photo
    if (
      myAvatarChanged ||
      myForm.avatarUrl !== (user.avatarUrl ?? '')
    ) {
      if (myAvatarFile && user.id) {
        const uploaded = await uploadMemberImage(
          myAvatarFile,
          user.id
        )

        updates.avatarUrl = uploaded.imageUrl
      } else if (myForm.avatarUrl === '') {
        updates.avatarUrl = ''
        photoRemovedFromStorage = Boolean(user.avatarUrl)
      } else if (!myForm.avatarUrl.startsWith('data:')) {
        updates.avatarUrl = myForm.avatarUrl
      } else {
        setError(
          'The profile photo has not finished uploading. Please select it again.'
        )
        return
      }
    }

    if (Object.keys(updates).length === 0) {
      setError('No changes to save.')
      return
    }

    // Save credentials
    await updateMyCredentials(updates)

    // Remove old profile image if necessary
    if (photoRemovedFromStorage) {
      await deleteMemberImage(
        getMemberImagePath(user.id)
      ).catch(() => {})
    }

    // Clear password fields
    setMyForm((prev) => ({
      ...prev,
      password: '',
      confirmPassword: '',
      currentPassword: '',
    }))

    setMyAvatarFile(null)
    setMyAvatarChanged(false)

    // IMPORTANT: successful save state
    setSavingCredentials(false)
    setCredentialsSaved(true)
    setSuccess('Your credentials updated successfully.')

    refresh()

    // Return to normal button after 2 seconds
    window.setTimeout(() => {
      setCredentialsSaved(false)
    }, 2000)

  } catch (err) {
    setSavingCredentials(false)

    setError(
      err instanceof Error
        ? err.message
        : 'Failed to update credentials'
    )
  }
}

  return (
    <div className="space-y-6">
      <div>
        <h2 className="text-xl font-bold text-slate-900">Admin Management</h2>
        <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-slate-500">Manage admin accounts and credentials. Only one Main Admin exists at a time.</p>
      </div>

      {(error || success) && (
        <div className={`rounded-xl border px-4 py-3 text-sm ${error ? 'border-red-200 bg-red-50 text-red-700' : 'border-emerald-200 bg-emerald-50 text-emerald-700'}`}>
          {error || success}
        </div>
      )}

      <div className="rounded-[20px] border border-orange-100 bg-white p-5">
        <div className="mb-4 flex items-center gap-2">
          <UserCog size={18} className="text-orange-600" />
          <h3 className="text-lg font-bold text-slate-900">My Credentials</h3>
          {user?.isMainAdmin && (
            <span className="ml-auto flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full bg-amber-100 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-bold text-amber-700">
              <Crown size={12} /> Main Admin
            </span>
          )}
        </div>
        <div className="space-y-3">
          <AvatarUpload
            key={myForm.avatarUrl || 'empty-avatar'}
            currentImageUrl={myForm.avatarUrl}
            onImageSelected={(file, previewUrl) => {
              setMyForm((prev) => ({ ...prev, avatarUrl: previewUrl }))
              setMyAvatarFile(file)
              setMyAvatarChanged(true)
            }}
            onImageRemoved={() => {
              setMyForm((prev) => ({ ...prev, avatarUrl: '' }))
              setMyAvatarFile(null)
              setMyAvatarChanged(true)
            }}
            label="My Profile Photo"
            userId={user?.id}
          />
          <div>
            <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">Name</label>
            <input value={myForm.name} onChange={(e) => setMyForm({ ...myForm, name: e.target.value })} className="w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400" />
          </div>
          <div>
            <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">Username (login identifier — must be unique)</label>
            <input
              value={myForm.username}
              onChange={(e) => setMyForm({ ...myForm, username: e.target.value })}
              className="w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400"
            />
            {myForm.username && validateUsername(myForm.username) && (
              <p className="mt-1 flex items-center gap-1 text-[11px] font-semibold text-red-600"><AlertCircle size={11} /> {validateUsername(myForm.username)}</p>
            )}
          </div>
          <div>
            <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">Email</label>
            <input type="email" value={myForm.email} onChange={(e) => setMyForm({ ...myForm, email: e.target.value })} className="w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400" />
          </div>
          <div>
            <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">Phone Number (exactly 10 digits — login identifier)</label>
            <input
              value={myForm.phone}
              onChange={(e) => setMyForm({ ...myForm, phone: e.target.value })}
              placeholder="9876543210"
              inputMode="numeric"
              maxLength={10}
              className={`w-full rounded-lg border px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400 ${myForm.phone && !isValidPhone(myForm.phone) ? 'border-red-300 bg-red-50' : 'border-slate-200'}`}
            />
            {myForm.phone && !isValidPhone(myForm.phone) && (
              <p className="mt-1 flex items-center gap-1 text-[11px] font-semibold text-red-600"><AlertCircle size={11} /> Phone number must be exactly 10 digits (digits only — no +91, no spaces).</p>
            )}
          </div>
          {myForm.password.length > 0 && (
            <div>
              <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">Current Password (required to change password)</label>
              <input
                type="password"
                value={myForm.currentPassword}
                onChange={(e) => setMyForm({ ...myForm, currentPassword: e.target.value })}
                autoComplete="current-password"
                className="w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400"
              />
            </div>
          )}
          <div>
            <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">New Password (leave blank to keep current)</label>
            <input type="password" value={myForm.password} onChange={(e) => setMyForm({ ...myForm, password: e.target.value })} placeholder="Strong password" className="w-full rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400" />
            <PasswordChecklist password={myForm.password} confirm={myForm.confirmPassword} />
          </div>
          <div>
            <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">Confirm New Password</label>
            <input
              type="password"
              value={myForm.confirmPassword}
              onChange={(e) => setMyForm({ ...myForm, confirmPassword: e.target.value })}
              placeholder="Re-enter password"
              className={`w-full rounded-lg border px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400 ${myForm.confirmPassword && myForm.confirmPassword !== myForm.password ? 'border-red-300 bg-red-50' : 'border-slate-200'}`}
            />
          </div>
          <button
  onClick={handleUpdateMe}
  disabled={
    savingCredentials ||
    credentialsSaved ||
    (myForm.password.length > 0 &&
      (!validatePassword(myForm.password).isValid ||
        myForm.confirmPassword !== myForm.password))
  }
  title={
    myForm.password.length > 0 &&
    myForm.confirmPassword !== myForm.password
      ? 'Passwords do not match'
      : undefined
  }
  className={`flex items-center gap-2 rounded-xl px-4 py-2.5 text-sm font-bold text-white transition ${
    credentialsSaved
      ? 'bg-emerald-500'
      : 'bg-orange-500 hover:bg-orange-600'
  } disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-60`}
>
  {savingCredentials ? (
    'Saving…'
  ) : credentialsSaved ? (
    <>
      <CheckCircle2 size={16} />
      Saved
    </>
  ) : (
    <>
      <CheckCircle size={16} />
      Save Changes
    </>
  )}
</button>
        </div>
      </div>

      <div className="rounded-[20px] border border-orange-100 bg-white p-5">
        <div className="mb-4 flex items-center justify-between">
          <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
            <Shield size={18} className="text-orange-600" />
            <h3 className="text-lg font-bold text-slate-900">All Admins ({admins.length}/{MAX_ADMINS})</h3>
          </div>
          {isMainAdmin && !adminsFull && (
            <button onClick={() => setShowCreate(!showCreate)} className="flex items-center gap-1.5 rounded-xl bg-orange-100 px-3 py-2 text-sm font-bold text-orange-700 transition hover:bg-orange-200">
              {showCreate ? <X size={16} /> : <Plus size={16} />}
              {showCreate ? 'Cancel' : 'Add Admin'}
            </button>
          )}
        </div>

        {isMainAdmin && adminsFull && (
          <p className="mb-4 flex items-center gap-2 rounded-xl border border-amber-200 bg-amber-50 px-3 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-amber-700">
            <AlertCircle size={14} /> Admin limit reached ({admins.length}/{MAX_ADMINS}). Delete or demote an admin before creating a new one.
          </p>
        )}

        {showCreate && (
          <div className="mb-4 rounded-xl border border-orange-200 bg-orange-50 p-4">
            <h4 className="mb-3 text-sm font-bold text-slate-800">Create New Admin</h4>
            <p className="mb-3 text-xs text-slate-500">Maximum {MAX_ADMINS} admins allowed. Currently {admins.length}/{MAX_ADMINS}.</p>
            <div className="mb-3">
              <AvatarUpload
                currentImageUrl={form.avatarUrl}
                onImageSelected={(file, previewUrl) => { setForm({ ...form, avatarUrl: previewUrl }); setFormAvatarFile(file) }}
                onImageRemoved={() => { setForm({ ...form, avatarUrl: '' }); setFormAvatarFile(null) }}
                label="Admin Profile Photo"
              />
            </div>
            <div className="grid grid-cols-1 gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2">
              <input value={form.name} onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, name: e.target.value })} placeholder="Full name" className="rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400" />
              <input value={form.username} onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, username: e.target.value })} placeholder="Username (unique login identifier)" className="rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400" />
              <input value={form.email} onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, email: e.target.value })} placeholder="Email address" type="email" className="rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400" />
              <input
                value={form.phone}
                onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, phone: e.target.value })}
                placeholder="Phone number (10 digits)"
                inputMode="numeric"
                maxLength={10}
                className={`rounded-lg border px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400 ${form.phone && !isValidPhone(form.phone) ? 'border-red-300 bg-red-50' : 'border-slate-200'}`}
              />
              <input value={form.password} onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, password: e.target.value })} placeholder="Strong password" type="password" className="rounded-lg border border-slate-200 px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400" />
            </div>
            <div className="mt-3">
              <PasswordChecklist password={form.password} confirm={form.confirmPassword} />
            </div>
            <div className="mt-3">
              <label className="mb-1 block text-xs font-semibold text-slate-600">Confirm Password</label>
              <input
                value={form.confirmPassword}
                onChange={(e) => setForm({ ...form, confirmPassword: e.target.value })}
                placeholder="Re-enter password"
                type="password"
                className={`w-full rounded-lg border px-3 py-2 text-sm outline-none focus:border-orange-400 ${form.confirmPassword && form.confirmPassword !== form.password ? 'border-red-300 bg-red-50' : 'border-slate-200'}`}
              />
            </div>
            <button
  onClick={handleCreate}
  disabled={
    creating ||
    created ||
    !form.name ||
    !form.username ||
    !form.email ||
    !isValidPhone(form.phone) ||
    !validatePassword(form.password).isValid ||
    form.confirmPassword !== form.password
  }
  title={
    form.confirmPassword !== form.password
      ? 'Passwords do not match'
      : undefined
  }
  className={`mt-3 flex items-center gap-2 rounded-xl px-4 py-2.5 text-sm font-bold text-white transition ${
    created
      ? 'bg-emerald-500'
      : 'bg-orange-500 hover:bg-orange-600'
  } disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-60`}
>
  {creating ? (
    'Creating…'
  ) : created ? (
    <>
      <CheckCircle2 size={16} />
      Created
    </>
  ) : (
    <>
      <Plus size={16} />
      Create Admin
    </>
  )}
</button>
          </div>
        )}

        {admins.length === 0 ? (
          <p className="text-sm text-slate-500">No admins yet.</p>
        ) : (
          <div className="space-y-2">
            {admins.map((admin) => (
              <div key={admin.id} className="flex min-w-0 flex-col gap-3 rounded-xl border border-slate-100 bg-slate-50 px-3 py-3 sm:flex-row sm:items-center sm:justify-between sm:px-4">
                <button
                  onClick={() => setDetailsAdmin(admin)}
                  className="flex min-w-0 items-center gap-3 text-left"
                  title="View details"
                >
                  <Avatar name={admin.name} src={admin.avatarUrl} role="admin" className="h-9 w-9 text-sm" />
                  <div className="min-w-0">
                    <p className="text-sm font-semibold text-slate-900">{admin.name}</p>
                    <p className="max-w-full truncate text-xs text-slate-500">{admin.email} {admin.phone ? `• ${admin.phone}` : ''}</p>
                  </div>
                </button>
                <div className="flex w-full flex-wrap items-center gap-2 sm:w-auto sm:justify-end">
                  {admin.isMainAdmin ? (
                    <span className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full bg-amber-100 px-2.5 py-1 text-xs font-bold text-amber-700">
                      <Crown size={12} /> Main Admin
                    </span>
                  ) : (
                    <>
                      {isMainAdmin && (
                        <button onClick={() => setShowTransfer(showTransfer === admin.id ? null : admin.id)} className="flex min-w-0 flex-1 items-center justify-center gap-1 rounded-lg bg-amber-100 px-2.5 py-1.5 text-xs font-bold text-amber-700 transition hover:bg-amber-200 sm:flex-none">
                          <Crown size={12} /> <span className="truncate">Transfer Title</span>
                        </button>
                      )}
                      {user?.id !== admin.id && (
                        <button
  onClick={() => handleDelete(admin.id)}
  className="rounded-lg bg-red-50 p-2 text-red-500 transition hover:bg-red-100"
  title="Delete admin"
  aria-label={`Delete ${admin.name}`}
>
  <Trash2 size={14} />
</button>
                      )}
                    </>
                  )}
                </div>
              </div>
            ))}
          </div>
        )}

        {showTransfer && (
          <div className="mt-3 rounded-xl border border-amber-200 bg-amber-50 p-4">
            <p className="mb-2 text-sm font-semibold text-amber-800">Transfer Main Admin title?</p>
            <p className="mb-3 text-xs text-amber-700">You will become a regular Admin. This action cannot be undone unless the new Main Admin transfers it back.</p>
            <div className="flex gap-2">
              <button onClick={() => { const a = admins.find((x) => x.id === showTransfer); if (a) handleTransfer(a.id, a.name) }} className="rounded-lg bg-amber-500 px-3 py-2 text-xs font-bold text-white hover:bg-amber-600">
                Confirm Transfer
              </button>
              <button onClick={() => setShowTransfer(null)} className="rounded-lg border border-slate-200 bg-white px-3 py-2 text-xs font-bold text-slate-600 hover:bg-slate-50">
                Cancel
              </button>
            </div>
          </div>
        )}
      </div>

      {/* Admin Details Modal — opened by clicking the avatar / row */}
      {detailsAdmin && (
        <div
          className="fixed inset-0 z-60 flex items-start justify-center overflow-y-auto overscroll-contain bg-black/40 p-4 py-6 sm:items-center bh-modal-overlay"
          onClick={() => setDetailsAdmin(null)}
        >
          <div
            className="w-full max-w-sm rounded-3xl bg-white p-6 shadow-2xl"
            onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
          >
            <div className="mb-4 flex items-start justify-between">
              <h3 className="text-xl font-bold text-slate-900">Admin Details</h3>
              <button
                onClick={() => setDetailsAdmin(null)}
                className="rounded-lg p-1.5 text-slate-400 transition hover:bg-slate-100 hover:text-slate-600"
                aria-label="Close"
              >
                <X size={18} />
              </button>
            </div>

            <div className="flex flex-col items-center text-center">
              <Avatar
                name={detailsAdmin.name}
                src={detailsAdmin.avatarUrl}
                role="admin"
                className="h-24 w-24 text-3xl"
              />
              <p className="mt-3 text-lg font-bold text-slate-900">{detailsAdmin.name}</p>
              <span className="mt-1 flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full bg-orange-100 px-2.5 py-0.5 text-[11px] font-bold text-orange-700 capitalize">
                {detailsAdmin.isMainAdmin ? 'Main Admin' : 'Admin'}
              </span>
            </div>

            <div className="mt-5 space-y-2.5 text-sm">
              <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-slate-600">
                <Mail size={15} className="shrink-0 text-slate-400" />
                {detailsAdmin.email}
              </div>
              {detailsAdmin.phone && (
                <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-slate-600">
                  <Phone size={15} className="shrink-0 text-slate-400" />
                  {detailsAdmin.phone}
                </div>
              )}
              <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-slate-600">
                <BadgeCheck size={15} className="shrink-0 text-slate-400" />
                <span className="capitalize">{detailsAdmin.id}</span>
              </div>
              <div className="flex items-center gap-2 text-slate-600">
                <Calendar size={15} className="shrink-0 text-slate-400" />
                {new Date(detailsAdmin.createdAt).toLocaleDateString('en-IN', {
                  day: 'numeric',
                  month: 'short',
                  year: 'numeric',
                })}
              </div>
            </div>

            {detailsAdmin.isMainAdmin && (
              <div className="mt-3 flex items-center justify-center">
                <span className="flex items-center gap-1 rounded-full bg-amber-100 px-2.5 py-1 text-[11px] font-bold text-amber-700">
                  <Crown size={12} /> Main Admin
                </span>
              </div>
            )}
          </div>
        </div>
      )}

      {deleteCandidate && (
  <div
    className="fixed inset-0 z-70 flex items-center justify-center bg-black/40 p-4"
    onClick={() => !deleting && setDeleteCandidate(null)}
  >
    <div
      className="w-full max-w-md rounded-2xl bg-white p-6 shadow-2xl"
      onClick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
    >
      <div className="mb-4 flex items-start justify-between">
        <div>
          <h3 className="text-lg font-bold text-slate-900">
            Delete Admin?
          </h3>
          <p className="mt-1 text-sm text-slate-500">
            Are you sure you want to delete this admin account?
          </p>
        </div>

        <button
          onClick={() => !deleting && setDeleteCandidate(null)}
          className="rounded-lg p-1.5 text-slate-400 transition hover:bg-slate-100 hover:text-slate-600"
          disabled={deleting}
        >
          <X size={18} />
        </button>
      </div>

      <div className="mb-5 rounded-xl border border-red-200 bg-red-50 p-3">
        <p className="text-sm font-bold text-red-700">
          {deleteCandidate.name}
        </p>
        <p className="mt-1 text-xs text-red-600">
          {deleteCandidate.email}
        </p>
        <p className="mt-2 text-xs font-semibold text-red-600">
          This action cannot be undone.
        </p>
      </div>

      <div className="flex justify-end gap-2">
        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={() => setDeleteCandidate(null)}
          disabled={deleting}
          className="rounded-xl border border-slate-200 bg-white px-4 py-2.5 text-sm font-semibold text-slate-600 transition hover:bg-slate-50 disabled:opacity-50"
        >
          Cancel
        </button>

        <button
          type="button"
          onClick={confirmDelete}
          disabled={deleting}
          className="flex items-center gap-2 rounded-xl bg-red-500 px-4 py-2.5 text-sm font-bold text-white transition hover:bg-red-600 disabled:cursor-not-allowed disabled:opacity-60"
        >
          {deleting ? (
            'Deleting…'
          ) : (
            <>
              <Trash2 size={15} />
              Delete Admin
            </>
          )}
        </button>
      </div>
    </div>
  </div>
)}
    </div>
  )
}
