// Firebase Authentication service (real implementation).
// Login/accounts/roles are owned by Firebase Auth + the `users` Firestore doc.
//
// Important: the SDK handles are resolved LAZILY. The previous version called
// `getAuthNow()!` at module scope, which is null whenever Firebase is not
// configured — any import in mock mode then crashed at load time.
import { signInWithEmailAndPassword, signOut as fbSignOut, onAuthStateChanged, sendPasswordResetEmail, updateEmail as fbUpdateEmail, type User } from 'firebase/auth'
import { collection, getDocs, doc, getDoc, setDoc } from 'firebase/firestore'
import { getAuthNow, getFirestoreNow } from '../../firebase'
import { isFirebaseConfigured } from './config'
import {
  DESIGNATED_MAIN_ADMIN_EMAIL,
  ensureDesignatedMainAdmin,
  markBootstrapClaimed,
  repairAuthIdentity,
  resolveAuthEmailForIdentifier,
  isValidContactEmailFormat,
} from './userService'
import { looksLikeEmail, normalizeUsername, internalEmailForUsername, INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_DOMAIN } from '../../lib/username'

// Password recovery is owned by Firebase Authentication: the SDK emails a signed
// reset link. This application never mints, stores or verifies its own reset
// codes, and it never sees the new password.

/**
 * Ask Firebase Authentication to email a password-reset link.
 * Resolves for any well-formed address (Firebase does not disclose whether an
 * account exists); rejects with a mapped message for invalid address / quota /
 * network failures.
 */
export const sendPasswordReset = async (email: string): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured.')
  try {
    await sendPasswordResetEmail(requireAuth(), email.trim().toLowerCase())
  } catch (err) {
    const code = (err as { code?: string })?.code
    if (code && String(code).startsWith('auth/')) throw new Error(mapAuthError(err))
    throw new Error('Password reset email could not be sent. Please try again.')
  }
}

export type Role = 'admin' | 'waiter' | 'supervisor'

export interface AuthUser {
  uid: string
  email: string
  displayName: string
  role: Role
  phone?: string
  avatarUrl?: string
  active: boolean
  /** Only the Main Admin can manage other admins / the whole directory. */
  isMainAdmin: boolean
  /** From the `users/{uid}` document (falls back to "now" when unavailable). */
  createdAt?: number
}

const requireAuth = () => {
  const auth = getAuthNow()
  if (!auth) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured. Use mock mode for development.')
  return auth
}

const toAuthUser = (data: {
  uid: string
  email?: string
  name?: string
  role?: string
  phone?: string
  avatarUrl?: string
  active?: boolean
  isMainAdmin?: boolean
  createdAt?: number
}): AuthUser => ({
  uid: data.uid,
  email: data.email ?? '',
  displayName: data.name ?? '',
  role: (data.role as Role) ?? 'waiter',
  phone: data.phone,
  avatarUrl: data.avatarUrl,
  active: data.active ?? true,
  isMainAdmin: data.isMainAdmin === true,
  createdAt: typeof data.createdAt === 'number' ? data.createdAt : Date.now(),
})

/**
 * Resolve the profile for a freshly signed-in Auth user:
 *  1. the `users/{uid}` document when it exists (normal path);
 *  2. otherwise adopt the matching email record from the directory — this heals
 *     accounts whose profile was created under a device-local id;
 *  3. otherwise self-provision a `waiter` profile — and ONLY for the nominated
 *     owner email, on a genuinely empty project, claim the one-time Main Admin
 *     bootstrap (see firestore.rules: `isDesignatedOwner` + `bootstrapUnclaimed`).
 */
const resolveProfile = async (
  uid: string,
  email: string,
  displayName?: string,
): Promise<AuthUser> => {
  const db = getFirestoreNow()
  if (!db) return toAuthUser({ uid, email, name: displayName })
  // One-time recovery for the nominated owner account. Best-effort: the account
  // must never fail to sign in because a recovery write was not permitted.
  await ensureDesignatedMainAdmin(uid, email).catch(() => {})

  // Best-effort self-heal: align the stored authEmail (users/{uid} + the
  // username/phone/email mappings this account owns) with the REAL Firebase
  // Auth identity that just authenticated. Repairs accounts whose stored
  // identity was malformed (e.g. "@beeshive.local") so username/phone login
  // resolves to the SAME Auth account as real-email login. Never touches
  // credentials and never depends on succeeding.
  await repairAuthIdentity(uid, email).catch(() => {})

  const own = await getDoc(doc(db, 'users', uid))
  if (own.exists()) {
    const d = own.data()
    return toAuthUser({
      uid,
      email: d.email ?? email,
      name: d.name ?? displayName ?? '',
      role: d.role,
      phone: d.phone,
      avatarUrl: d.avatarUrl,
      active: d.active,
      isMainAdmin: d.isMainAdmin === true,
      createdAt: typeof d.createdAt === 'number' ? d.createdAt : undefined,
    })
  }

  const fallback: Record<string, unknown> = {
    name: displayName || email.split('@')[0] || 'User',
    email,
    role: 'waiter',
    isMainAdmin: false,
    active: true,
    createdAt: Date.now(),
  }

  try {
    const all = await getDocs(collection(db, 'users'))
    const match = all.docs.find(
      (d) => String(d.data().email ?? '').toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase(),
    )
    let profile: Record<string, unknown>
    if (match) {
      profile = { ...match.data() }
    } else {
      // First sign-in of an account that has no `users/{uid}` document.
      //
      // Only the nominated OWNER email may claim the one-time Main Admin
      // bootstrap, and only while the collection is genuinely empty —
      // firestore.rules grants that single guarded path (see the
      // `counters/bootstrap` claim there). Every other account self-provisions
      // as a `waiter`, which is the only role the rules let a user give
      // themselves, so whoever signs in first on a fresh project can never
      // promote themselves to admin.
      const canBootstrap =
        all.empty && email.trim().toLowerCase() === DESIGNATED_MAIN_ADMIN_EMAIL
      profile = {
        ...fallback,
        role: canBootstrap ? 'admin' : 'waiter',
        isMainAdmin: canBootstrap,
      }
    }
    // `uid` is written explicitly (the document id IS the Auth uid) and always
    // wins over any legacy value copied from the directory record above.
    await setDoc(doc(db, 'users', uid), { ...profile, uid, updatedAt: Date.now() }, { merge: true })
    if (profile.isMainAdmin === true) await markBootstrapClaimed(uid)
    return toAuthUser({
      uid,
      email,
      name: String(profile.name ?? fallback.name),
      role: String(profile.role ?? 'waiter'),
      phone: profile.phone as string | undefined,
      avatarUrl: profile.avatarUrl as string | undefined,
      active: profile.active !== false,
      isMainAdmin: profile.isMainAdmin === true,
      createdAt: typeof profile.createdAt === 'number' ? profile.createdAt : undefined,
    })
  } catch {
    // The Auth identity is valid even when the profile document could not be
    // read/written (offline, rules). Never dump the raw Firebase error: fall
    // back to a minimal waiter profile and let the caller decide.
    return toAuthUser({ uid, email, name: String(fallback.name) })
  }
}

/**
 * Maps Firebase Auth error codes to clean user-facing messages.
 * Only handles `auth/*` codes; the default fallback covers everything else.
 * No secrets, tokens, or raw Firebase responses are ever exposed.
 */
export const mapAuthError = (error: unknown): string => {
  const code = (error as { code?: string })?.code
  switch (code) {
    case 'auth/invalid-credential':
    case 'auth/invalid-login-credentials':
    case 'auth/wrong-password':
    case 'auth/user-not-found':
      return 'Invalid username or password.'
    case 'auth/invalid-email':
      return 'Please enter a valid username.'
    case 'auth/missing-password':
      return 'Please enter your password.'
    case 'auth/user-disabled':
      return 'This account has been disabled. Contact an administrator.'
    case 'auth/operation-not-allowed':
      return 'Username/password sign-in is not enabled for this project. Ask an administrator to enable it in Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method.'
    case 'auth/too-many-requests':
      return 'Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.'
    case 'auth/network-request-failed':
      return 'Network error. Please check your connection and try again.'
    case 'auth/invalid-api-key':
    case 'auth/api-key-not-valid.-please-pass-a-valid-api-key.':
      return 'This app is not configured for the Firebase project. Ask an administrator to check the Firebase configuration.'
    case 'auth/quota-exceeded':
    case 'auth/internal-error':
      return 'Sign-in is temporarily unavailable. Please try again.'
    default:
      return 'Sign-in could not be completed. Please try again.'
  }
}

/** Sign in with email + password; returns the role stamped on the users doc. */
export const signInWithEmail = async (email: string, password: string): Promise<AuthUser> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured. Use mock mode for development.')
  try {
    const credential = await signInWithEmailAndPassword(requireAuth(), email, password)
    const profile = await resolveProfile(
      credential.user.uid,
      credential.user.email ?? email,
      credential.user.displayName ?? undefined,
    )
    if (!profile.active) throw new Error('This account is deactivated. Ask an admin to re-enable it.')
    return profile
  } catch (err) {
    // Only map Firebase Auth error codes; pass through application errors as-is.
    const code = (err as { code?: string })?.code
    if (code && String(code).startsWith('auth/')) {
      throw new Error(mapAuthError(err))
    }
    throw err
  }
}

/**
 * Sign in with username + password.
 *
 * The application authenticates with username + password. Firebase Authentication
 * is still the credential authority: every account owns a real Firebase Auth
 * identity whose email is an internal, non-routable address minted at account
 * creation (username@beeshive.local) and kept stable across renames.
 *
 * The typed username resolves through the `usernames/{username}` mapping to
 * the account's internal auth email — so a renamed username stops working and
 * the new one becomes valid immediately. Firebase Auth proves the identity;
 * the users/{uid} Firestore document supplies the application profile and role.
 */
export const signInWithUsername = async (username: string, password: string): Promise<AuthUser> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured. Use mock mode for development.')

  const normalized = normalizeUsername(username)
  const authEmail = await resolveAuthEmailForIdentifier(normalized)
  return signInWithEmail(authEmail ?? internalEmailForUsername(normalized), password)
}

/**
 * Sign in with ANY supported login identifier:
 *   • username         → usernames/{normalized} mapping;
 *   • contact email    → emails/{lowercase} mapping;
 *   • 10-digit phone   → phones/{phone} mapping.
 * The mapping carries the account's internal auth email; accounts with no
 * mapping (e.g. the nominated owner, whose Auth identity is a real mailbox)
 * fall back to a direct Auth sign-in with the typed email address.
 */
export const signInWithIdentifier = async (identifier: string, password: string): Promise<AuthUser> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured. Use mock mode for development.')

  const raw = (identifier ?? '').trim()
  if (!raw) throw new Error('Enter your username, email or phone number.')

  const authEmail = await resolveAuthEmailForIdentifier(raw)
  if (authEmail) return signInWithEmail(authEmail, password)

  // No mapping exists for this identifier. Legacy/nominated accounts whose
  // Auth identity IS the typed email can still sign in directly; everything
  // else must fail with an honest error (never a guessed account).
  if (looksLikeEmail(raw)) return signInWithEmail(raw.toLowerCase(), password)
  throw new Error('No account matches that username, email or phone number.')
}

export const signOut = async (): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  await fbSignOut(requireAuth())
}

export const getCurrentUser = (): AuthUser | null => {
  const auth = getAuthNow()
  const fbUser = auth?.currentUser
  if (!fbUser) return null
  return toAuthUser({ uid: fbUser.uid, email: fbUser.email ?? '', name: fbUser.displayName ?? '' })
}

export const onAuthStateChange = (callback: (user: AuthUser | null) => void): (() => void) => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return () => {}
  const auth = getAuthNow()
  if (!auth) return () => {}
  return onAuthStateChanged(auth, async (fbUser) => {
    if (!fbUser) {
      callback(null)
      return
    }
    try {
      callback(await resolveProfile(fbUser.uid, fbUser.email ?? '', fbUser.displayName ?? undefined))
    } catch {
      callback(toAuthUser({ uid: fbUser.uid, email: fbUser.email ?? '', name: fbUser.displayName ?? '' }))
    }
    // One-time identity migration (Issue 5): an account still carrying the
    // legacy internal `username@beeshive.local` Auth identity is re-pointed at
    // its real contact email right after a fresh sign-in, so Firebase's native
    // password reset (which emails the AUTH address) delivers to the operator's
    // actual inbox. Best-effort and never fatal: a fresh sign-in is recent, so
    // `updateEmail` is permitted; failures (contact email already claimed by
    // another Auth account, session too old) leave the account untouched and
    // are retried at the next sign-in. UID, username and phone login are
    // unchanged — the identifier mappings are re-pointed by repairAuthIdentity.
    void migrateInternalAuthIdentity(fbUser).catch(() => {})
  })
}

/**
 * Re-point a legacy internal Auth identity (`<username>@beeshive.local`) at the
 * account's real contact email. Same Firebase Auth user (same UID, no new
 * account), so username/phone/email login keep resolving to it — the
 * identifier mappings and `users/{uid}.authEmail` are re-pointed right after.
 *
 * Safety rules:
 *   • The contact email is read from the account's own `users/{uid}` profile.
 *   • If the contact email is already claimed by a DIFFERENT Auth account
 *     (`auth/email-already-in-use`), the migration is stopped WITHOUT
 *     overwriting or merging anything, and the conflict is recorded on the
 *     profile (`contactEmailConflict`) for the Main Admin to resolve.
 *   • Any other failure (e.g. `auth/requires-recent-login` on a restored
 *     session) is silently retried at the next fresh sign-in.
 */
const migrateInternalAuthIdentity = async (fbUser: User): Promise<void> => {
  const uid = fbUser.uid
  const current = (fbUser.email ?? '').trim().toLowerCase()
  if (!current.endsWith(`@${INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_DOMAIN}`)) return // already a real mailbox
  const db = getFirestoreNow()
  if (!db) return

  const snap = await getDoc(doc(db, 'users', uid)).catch(() => null)
  const contact = (((snap?.data() as { email?: string } | undefined)?.email ?? '') as string)
    .trim()
    .toLowerCase()
  if (!isValidContactEmailFormat(contact) || contact.endsWith(`@${INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_DOMAIN}`)) return

  try {
    await fbUpdateEmail(fbUser, contact)
    // The Auth email changed: align `users/{uid}.authEmail` and every
    // identifier mapping owned by THIS uid with the new Auth identity.
    await repairAuthIdentity(uid, contact)
  } catch (err) {
    const code = (err as { code?: string })?.code
    if (code === 'auth/email-already-in-use' && snap?.exists()) {
      // Conflict: that contact email belongs to another Auth account. Never
      // overwrite or merge — stop this migration and surface the conflict.
      await setDoc(
        doc(db, 'users', uid),
        { contactEmailConflict: contact, updatedAt: Date.now() },
        { merge: true },
      ).catch(() => {})
    }
    // Anything else (requires-recent-login, network) — retried next sign-in.
  }
}

/** Read all users (roles) for admin staff management. */
export const listFirebaseUsers = async (): Promise<AuthUser[]> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return []
  const db = getFirestoreNow()
  if (!db) return []
  const snap = await getDocs(collection(db, 'users'))
  return snap.docs.map((d) => toAuthUser({ uid: d.id, ...(d.data() as object) }))
}

// Firebase configuration — THE single authoritative configuration for Bee's Hive.
//
// Rules for this module:
//   • Every value comes from `.env` (`VITE_FIREBASE_*`). No project id, API key,
//     bucket or app id is ever hard-coded in TypeScript.
//   • This is the ONLY module that calls `initializeApp`, and it initializes all
//     four Firebase products from that one app:
//         Firebase App → Firebase Authentication → Cloud Firestore → Cloud Storage
//     A second app on the same config would silently split the Auth session (the
//     user appears signed out in one module and signed in in another) and can
//     point different features at different projects.
//   • The configuration is validated as ONE coherent project: the sender id
//     encoded in the app id (`1:<senderId>:web:<hash>`) must match
//     VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID, and the auth domain / storage bucket
//     must belong to VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID. A half-updated `.env` (only the
//     API key swapped) is therefore reported as misconfigured instead of
//     silently signing users into a different project.
import { initializeApp, getApps, getApp, type FirebaseApp } from 'firebase/app'
import { getFirestore, type Firestore } from 'firebase/firestore'
import { getAuth, type Auth } from 'firebase/auth'
import { getStorage, type FirebaseStorage } from 'firebase/storage'

const env = (name: string): string => (import.meta.env[name] ?? '').toString().trim()

export const firebaseConfig = {
  apiKey: env('VITE_FIREBASE_API_KEY'),
  authDomain: env('VITE_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN'),
  projectId: env('VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID'),
  storageBucket: env('VITE_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET'),
  messagingSenderId: env('VITE_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID'),
  appId: env('VITE_FIREBASE_APP_ID'),
  ...(env('VITE_FIREBASE_MEASUREMENT_ID')
    ? { measurementId: env('VITE_FIREBASE_MEASUREMENT_ID') }
    : {}),
}

/** The project the running build is bound to. Not a secret — safe to display. */
export const firebaseProjectId = firebaseConfig.projectId

/** Sender id encoded inside the app id (`1:<senderId>:web:<hash>`). */
const senderIdFromAppId = firebaseConfig.appId.split(':')[1] ?? ''

/**
 * True only when a COMPLETE, self-consistent Web app config is present. When the
 * app id does not belong to the configured project the config counts as broken,
 * so a partially updated `.env` can never mix two projects.
 */
export const isFirebaseConfigured = (): boolean => {
  const complete = Boolean(
    firebaseConfig.apiKey &&
    firebaseConfig.authDomain &&
    firebaseConfig.projectId &&
    firebaseConfig.storageBucket &&
    firebaseConfig.messagingSenderId &&
    firebaseConfig.appId
  )
  if (!complete) return false
  // Standard Firebase host/bucket names for the configured project. Both legacy
  // (`.appspot.com`) and current (`.firebasestorage.app`) bucket suffixes are
  // accepted so an existing project keeps working after a bucket migration.
  const sameProjectHost =
    firebaseConfig.authDomain === `${firebaseConfig.projectId}.firebaseapp.com` ||
    firebaseConfig.authDomain === `${firebaseConfig.projectId}.web.app`
  const sameProjectBucket =
    firebaseConfig.storageBucket === `${firebaseConfig.projectId}.firebasestorage.app` ||
    firebaseConfig.storageBucket === `${firebaseConfig.projectId}.appspot.com`
  return sameProjectHost && sameProjectBucket && senderIdFromAppId === firebaseConfig.messagingSenderId
}

interface FirebaseServices {
  app: FirebaseApp
  auth: Auth
  db: Firestore
  storage: FirebaseStorage
}

/** Memoized services for the single Firebase app of this page load. */
let services: FirebaseServices | null = null

const build = (): FirebaseServices | null => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return null
  try {
    // getApps()/getApp() guard: a hot reload or a second import must reuse the
    // already-initialized app instead of creating a duplicate "[DEFAULT]" app.
    const app = getApps().length ? getApp() : initializeApp(firebaseConfig)
    return {
      app,
      auth: getAuth(app),
      db: getFirestore(app),
      storage: getStorage(app),
    }
  } catch {
    // A malformed configuration must not crash the bundle: the app then runs
    // with Firebase unavailable and reports it through the normal error paths.
    return null
  }
}

export const getFirebaseServices = (): FirebaseServices | null => {
  if (!services) services = build()
  return services
}

export const getAppNow = (): FirebaseApp | null => getFirebaseServices()?.app ?? null
export const getAuthNow = (): Auth | null => getFirebaseServices()?.auth ?? null
export const getFirestoreNow = (): Firestore | null => getFirebaseServices()?.db ?? null
export const getStorageNow = (): FirebaseStorage | null => getFirebaseServices()?.storage ?? null

// Compatibility handles (null when Firebase is not configured). Kept so legacy
// imports keep working without creating a second initialization path.
export const app = getFirebaseServices()?.app ?? null
export const auth = getFirebaseServices()?.auth ?? null
export const db = getFirebaseServices()?.db ?? null
export const storage = getFirebaseServices()?.storage ?? null

/**
 * Data mode. PRODUCTION IS ALWAYS `firebase`.
 *
 * `mock` exists only for local development / automated UI work without a
 * Firebase project: it keeps business records in the browser, which is exactly
 * what production must never do. It is therefore hard-gated behind the Vite DEV
 * flag, so a built bundle (`npm run build` → `vite preview` / any deployment)
 * runs in Firebase mode even if `VITE_DATA_MODE=mock` is left in the
 * environment by mistake. No business data can end up in localStorage in a
 * deployed build.
 */
const requestedDataMode = import.meta.env.VITE_DATA_MODE || 'firebase'

export const dataMode: 'firebase' | 'mock' =
  import.meta.env.DEV && requestedDataMode === 'mock' ? 'mock' : 'firebase'

/**
 * Firestore data service — persistence for RestaurantContext + AuthContext.
 *
 * Every collection stores one document per entity (doc id = entity id).
 * Writes are BATCHED and CHUNKED (Firestore allows max 500 operations per
 * batch — a busy restaurant day can easily exceed that, so an unchunked batch
 * would start throwing mid-service). The context layer diffs its state and
 * sends only the entities that actually changed, so no full-collection read is
 * needed before a write.
 *
 * All functions are safe no-ops when Firebase is not configured (mock mode).
 */
import {
  collection,
  getDocs,
  doc,
  writeBatch,
  deleteDoc,
  onSnapshot,
  getDoc,
  setDoc,
  type DocumentData,
  type WriteBatch,
} from 'firebase/firestore'
import { getFirestoreNow } from '../../firebase'
import { isFirebaseConfigured } from './config'

const BATCH_LIMIT = 500

const db = () => getFirestoreNow()

const dangerousFields = ['__proto__', 'prototype', 'constructor']

export interface StoredEntity {
  id: string
}

export interface SaveOptions {
  /** Batch-delete remote docs missing from `items`. Firestore rules only let
   * admins delete most collections, so waiter/supervisor clients must pass
   * false (upsert only). */
  allowDeletes?: boolean
}

/**
 * Canonical Firestore collection names — keep in sync with firestore.rules.
 * Notes:
 *  • dining sessions live in "diningSessions" (that is the rules name);
 *  • menu categories live in "menuCategories" (restaurant-scoped);
 *  • settings is a single "settings/restaurant" document;
 *  • users is the staff/credential directory (passwords are never stored
 *    plaintext — see services/firebase/userService.ts).
 */
export const FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS = {
  orders: 'orders',
  sessions: 'diningSessions',
  tables: 'tables',
  menu: 'menu',
  categories: 'menuCategories',
  bills: 'bills',
  paymentRecords: 'paymentRecords',
  notifications: 'notifications',
  inventory: 'inventory',
  stockHistory: 'stockHistory',
  inventoryUsage: 'inventoryUsage',
  purchaseRequests: 'purchaseRequests',
  recipes: 'recipes',
  activityLog: 'activityLog',
  users: 'users',
  settings: 'settings',
  printJobs: 'printJobs',
  counters: 'counters',
  analytics: 'analytics',
} as const

export type FirestoreCollectionName =
  (typeof FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS)[keyof typeof FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS]

/**
 * Recursively remove everything Firestore rejects in a document payload:
 *   • `undefined` properties (any depth) — "Unsupported field value: undefined"
 *   • `undefined` entries inside arrays (Firestore cannot store a hole)
 *   • functions / symbols (unsupported value types)
 *   • prototype-pollution keys (`__proto__`, `prototype`, `constructor`)
 * BigInt values are normalised to Number because Firestore has no BigInt type.
 * Dates and plain primitives are passed through untouched.
 */
/**
 * Firestore SDK value objects (Timestamp, FieldValue sentinels such as
 * serverTimestamp()/increment()/arrayUnion(), DocumentReference, GeoPoint,
 * Bytes) are class instances. Rebuilding them as plain objects would silently
 * corrupt the field — a Timestamp would be stored as `{seconds, nanoseconds}`
 * — so only genuine plain objects are walked; every other object passes
 * through untouched.
 */
const isPlainObject = (value: object): boolean => {
  const proto = Object.getPrototypeOf(value)
  return proto === Object.prototype || proto === null
}

const strip = (value: unknown): unknown => {
  if (Array.isArray(value)) {
    return value.filter((item) => item !== undefined).map(strip)
  }
  if (value === null || typeof value !== 'object') return value
  if (value instanceof Date) return value
  // Firestore sentinels / SDK classes / custom class instances — keep as-is
  // instead of flattening them into a plain object.
  if (!isPlainObject(value)) return value
  const out: Record<string, unknown> = {}
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(value)) {
    if (dangerousFields.includes(k) || v === undefined) continue
    if (typeof v === 'function' || typeof v === 'symbol') continue
    out[k] = typeof v === 'bigint' ? Number(v) : strip(v)
  }
  return out
}

/** A document payload is only writable when it is a plain object with a valid id. */
const writableEntity = (item: unknown): item is StoredEntity =>
  typeof item === 'object' && item !== null && typeof (item as StoredEntity).id === 'string' && (item as StoredEntity).id.length > 0

/** Commits write operations in Firestore-sized chunks (max 500 ops per batch). */
const commitInChunks = async (
  operations: { write: (batch: WriteBatch) => void }[],
): Promise<void> => {
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return
  for (let i = 0; i < operations.length; i += BATCH_LIMIT) {
    const batch = writeBatch(database)
    operations.slice(i, i + BATCH_LIMIT).forEach((op) => op.write(batch))
    await batch.commit()
  }
}

/**
 * Write only the entities that changed and (optionally) delete ids that
 * disappeared. Returns the number of documents written.
 */
export const saveEntities = async <T extends StoredEntity>(
  name: string,
  upserts: T[],
  deletes: string[] = [],
): Promise<number> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return 0
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return 0
  if (upserts.length === 0 && deletes.length === 0) return 0

  const col = collection(database, name)
  // `doc(col, undefined)` throws before Firestore can sanitise anything, so drop
  // any entity without a usable id first — the payload itself is always passed
  // through `strip()` so no `undefined` ever reaches the SDK.
  const safeUpserts = upserts.filter(writableEntity)
  const safeDeletes = deletes.filter((id) => typeof id === 'string' && id.length > 0)
  const ops = [
    ...safeUpserts.map((item) => ({
      write: (batch: WriteBatch) => batch.set(doc(col, item.id), (strip(item) ?? {}) as DocumentData),
    })),
    ...safeDeletes.map((id) => ({
      write: (batch: WriteBatch) => batch.delete(doc(col, id)),
    })),
  ]

  try {
    await commitInChunks(ops)
  } catch (err) {
    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
    if (import.meta.env.DEV) console.error(`Firestore save failed on "${name}":`, message)
    throw err
  }
  return safeUpserts.length + safeDeletes.length
}

/**
 * Replace the full contents of a collection with `items`.
 * Kept for compatibility; the live app uses `saveEntities` with a local diff so
 * it never needs the read below.
 */
export const saveCollection = async <T extends StoredEntity>(
  name: string,
  items: T[],
  options: SaveOptions = {},
): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return
  const { allowDeletes = true } = options
  let deletes: string[] = []
  if (allowDeletes) {
    const existing = await getDocs(collection(database, name))
    const keep = new Set(items.map((i) => i.id))
    deletes = existing.docs.filter((d) => !keep.has(d.id)).map((d) => d.id)
  }
  await saveEntities(name, items, deletes)
}

export const loadCollection = async <T extends StoredEntity>(name: string): Promise<T[]> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return []
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return []
  const snap = await getDocs(collection(database, name))
  return snap.docs.map((d) => ({ id: d.id, ...(d.data() as object) }) as T)
}

/**
 * Live subscription to a collection — fires immediately with the current remote
 * contents and again on every change from ANY device. Returns an unsubscribe
 * function (no-op when Firebase is not configured).
 */
export const watchCollection = <T extends StoredEntity>(
  name: string,
  onChange: (items: T[]) => void,
): (() => void) => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return () => {}
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return () => {}
  return onSnapshot(
    collection(database, name),
    (snap) => onChange(snap.docs.map((d) => ({ id: d.id, ...(d.data() as object) }) as T)),
    (err) => {
      if (import.meta.env.DEV) console.error(`Firestore watch failed on "${name}":`, err.message)
    },
  )
}

export const deleteEntity = async (name: string, id: string): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return
  await deleteDoc(doc(collection(database, name), id))
}

/** Single-document read/write (settings live in `settings/restaurant`). */
export const loadDoc = async <T>(name: string, id: string): Promise<T | null> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return null
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return null
  const snap = await getDoc(doc(database, name, id))
  return snap.exists() ? (snap.data() as T) : null
}

export const saveDoc = async (name: string, id: string, data: unknown, options: { merge?: boolean } = {}): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  const database = db()
  if (!database) return
  try {
    const sanitized = strip(data)
    const payload = (sanitized && typeof sanitized === 'object' ? sanitized : {}) as DocumentData
    await setDoc(doc(database, name, id), payload, options)
  } catch (err) {
    const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
    if (import.meta.env.DEV) console.error(`Firestore doc save failed on "${name}/${id}":`, message)
    throw err
  }
}

/**
 * Durable print-job records (Firestore `printJobs` collection).
 *
 * The in-browser PrintQueue is operational state only; every status transition
 * is mirrored here so the authoritative print history survives a browser
 * refresh, a crashed tab or a different device. This record NEVER causes a
 * physical print — the relay's idempotency ledger remains the sole duplicate
 * protection, and reprints still go through the user-initiated new-job path.
 */
import { dataMode, isFirebaseConfigured } from './config'
import { FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS, saveDoc } from './dataService'

export interface DurablePrintJob {
  jobId: string
  kind: string
  printer: string
  referenceId: string
  status: 'QUEUED' | 'PRINTING' | 'PRINTED' | 'FAILED'
  createdAt: number
  updatedAt: number
  printedAt?: number
  attempts: number
  error?: string
  /** Light metadata only — never receipt contents or customer PII beyond refs. */
  tokenNumber?: number
  billNumber?: string
}

/** Fire-and-forget mirror of a print-job status transition into Firestore. */
export const persistPrintJob = (job: DurablePrintJob): void => {
  if (dataMode !== 'firebase' || !isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  // Firestore `printJobs` is the durable print history (never localStorage /
  // in-memory only). Failures are non-fatal: the physical print has already
  // been handed to the relay, and the job is retried on the next transition.
  saveDoc(FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.printJobs, job.jobId, job, { merge: true }).catch(() => {})
}

/** Extract the light metadata fields from a typed print payload. */
export const printJobMetadata = (payload: unknown): { tokenNumber?: number; billNumber?: string } => {
  if (payload && typeof payload === 'object') {
    const p = payload as { tokenNumber?: unknown; billNumber?: unknown }
    return {
      tokenNumber: typeof p.tokenNumber === 'number' ? p.tokenNumber : undefined,
      billNumber: typeof p.billNumber === 'string' ? p.billNumber : undefined,
    }
  }
  return {}
}


============================================================
FILE: src\services\firebase\sessionCapacityService.ts
============================================================

/**
 * Authoritative table-capacity enforcement for dining sessions.
 *
 * A table's `capacity` is the maximum TOTAL number of guests seated across ALL
 * active sessions on that table. One physical table may therefore host several
 * INDEPENDENT sessions (T-01, capacity 4 → session A 2 guests + session B 2
 * guests). `RestaurantContext.getTableOccupancy()` computes that for the UI, but
 * the UI is only UX: two waiters can act at the very same instant.
 *
 * `reserveSession()` is the authoritative check. It runs inside ONE Firestore
 * transaction that:
 *
 *   1. reads the table document (its `capacity`);
 *   2. reads `counters/tableCapacity_<tableId>`, a derived ledger that stores
 *      `occupancy` (sessionId → guest count) for the sessions currently using
 *      the table. Concurrent waiters read AND write this single document, which
 *      makes Firestore serialise them: the loser is retried, re-reads the ledger
 *      and therefore sees the session the winner just committed;
 *   3. re-reads every one of those session documents BY REFERENCE inside the same
 *      transaction, so the verdict comes from the authoritative
 *      `diningSessions` records and any concurrent change to them also forces a
 *      retry. Sessions whose status is `closed` (the application's existing
 *      lifecycle — no new status is introduced) or that no longer exist are
 *      dropped, so completing a session frees its seats immediately;
 *   4. rejects with `SessionCapacityExceededError` when the new session would
 *      push the table over capacity, otherwise writes the session document, the
 *      ledger and the table status in the same atomic commit.
 *
 * `occupancy` is a derived SUMMARY of real session documents, verified on every
 * reservation, so it can never hold a stale verdict: 2 + 2 + 2 guests on a
 * 4-seat table is impossible, and completed sessions never block a new one.
 *
 * Offline behaviour: a Firestore transaction needs the backend. When the device
 * is offline the reservation reports `authoritative: false` and the caller keeps
 * the application's existing offline-first path (local state + sync-engine push
 * on reconnect) — session creation is never blocked by a flaky connection.
 */
import { collection, doc, getDocs, query, runTransaction, where, type DocumentData } from 'firebase/firestore'
import { getFirestoreNow } from '../../firebase'
import { isFirebaseConfigured } from './config'
import { FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS } from './dataService'
import type { Session } from '../../context/RestaurantContext'

/**
 * Session statuses that no longer occupy a table. Mirrors the existing
 * `SessionStatus` lifecycle (`'active' | 'payment_pending' | 'closed'`) and the
 * `status !== 'closed'` filter used by `getActiveSessionsForTable()`. Completed
 * sessions free their seats again.
 */
const CLOSED_SESSION_STATUS = 'closed'

/** Ledger document id for one physical table (`counters/tableCapacity_<id>`). */
export const tableCapacityLedgerId = (tableId: string): string => `tableCapacity_${tableId}`

/**
 * Raised when a new session would push the combined guest count of a table past
 * its capacity. The message is written for the operator (it is shown as-is in
 * the session dialog).
 */
export class SessionCapacityExceededError extends Error {
  readonly capacity: number
  readonly occupied: number
  readonly requested: number
  readonly available: number

  constructor(capacity: number, occupied: number, requested: number) {
    const available = Math.max(0, capacity - occupied)
    super(
      `Only ${available} of ${capacity} seat(s) left on this table, but ${requested} guest(s) were requested.`,
    )
    this.name = 'SessionCapacityExceededError'
    this.capacity = capacity
    this.occupied = occupied
    this.requested = requested
    this.available = available
  }
}

/** True for genuine connectivity failures (no backend round trip possible). */
export const isOfflineFirestoreError = (err: unknown): boolean => {
  const code = (err as { code?: unknown } | null)?.code
  return code === 'unavailable' || code === 'deadline-exceeded'
}

export interface SessionReservation {
  /** true when the Firestore transaction ran — capacity was enforced server-side. */
  authoritative: boolean
}

interface StoredSessionShape {
  status?: unknown
  guestCount?: unknown
}

/** sessionId → guest count of the sessions that currently occupy a table. */
type OccupancyMap = Record<string, number>

/** Derived state kept in `counters/tableCapacity_<tableId>`. */
interface CapacityLedger {
  tableId?: unknown
  capacity?: unknown
  occupiedGuests?: unknown
  activeSessions?: unknown
  occupancy?: OccupancyMap
  updatedAt?: unknown
}

const asCount = (value: unknown): number => {
  const parsed = Math.floor(Number(value))
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) && parsed > 0 ? parsed : 0
}

const ledgerOccupancy = (ledger: CapacityLedger | undefined): OccupancyMap =>
  ledger?.occupancy && typeof ledger.occupancy === 'object' ? ledger.occupancy : {}

/**
 * Session ids that MIGHT occupy a table, read once from `diningSessions`.
 *
 * Only used to reconcile records that were created before this ledger existed
 * (or by any other write path): every candidate is then verified by reference
 * inside the transaction, so the verdict itself never depends on this read.
 */
const discoverOccupyingSessionIds = async (
  tableId: string,
  database: import('firebase/firestore').Firestore,
): Promise<string[]> => {
  const snapshot = await getDocs(
    query(collection(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.sessions), where('tableId', '==', tableId)),
  )
  return snapshot.docs
    .filter((stored) => (stored.data() as StoredSessionShape).status !== CLOSED_SESSION_STATUS)
    .map((stored) => stored.id)
}

/**
 * Read every candidate session document BY REFERENCE inside the transaction and
 * keep only the ones that still occupy the table.
 *
 * By-reference reads are part of the transaction's read set, so a concurrent
 * change to any of them makes Firestore retry the whole transaction — which is
 * what stops two waiters from overfilling a table together.
 */
const verifyOccupancy = async (
  transaction: import('firebase/firestore').Transaction,
  database: import('firebase/firestore').Firestore,
  candidateIds: string[],
  ledgerMap: OccupancyMap,
): Promise<{ occupancy: OccupancyMap; occupied: number; activeCount: number }> => {
  const ids = Array.from(new Set([...candidateIds, ...Object.keys(ledgerMap)]))
  const occupancy: OccupancyMap = {}
  let occupied = 0
  for (const id of ids) {
    const snapshot = await transaction.get(doc(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.sessions, id))
    // A session that is gone no longer occupies the table.
    if (!snapshot.exists()) continue
    const stored = snapshot.data() as StoredSessionShape
    // Completed / cancelled sessions free their seats (existing lifecycle).
    if (stored.status === CLOSED_SESSION_STATUS) continue
    const guests = asCount(stored.guestCount ?? ledgerMap[id])
    occupancy[id] = guests
    occupied += guests
  }
  return { occupancy, occupied, activeCount: Object.keys(occupancy).length }
}

/**
 * Atomically reserve the seats of a new session and persist the session itself.
 *
 * Throws `SessionCapacityExceededError` when the table does not have enough
 * remaining capacity — in that case NOTHING is written, so an invalid session
 * can never reach the database.
 */
export const reserveSession = async (session: Session): Promise<SessionReservation> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return { authoritative: false }
  const database = getFirestoreNow()
  if (!database) return { authoritative: false }

  const guests = asCount(session.guestCount)
  const tableRef = doc(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.tables, session.tableId)
  const ledgerRef = doc(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.counters, tableCapacityLedgerId(session.tableId))
  const sessionRef = doc(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.sessions, session.id)

  let candidateIds: string[]
  try {
    candidateIds = await discoverOccupyingSessionIds(session.tableId, database)
  } catch (err) {
    // Without the backend the transaction below cannot run either; the caller
    // keeps the app's existing offline-first behaviour.
    if (isOfflineFirestoreError(err)) return { authoritative: false }
    throw err
  }

  try {
    await runTransaction(database, async (transaction) => {
      const tableSnap = await transaction.get(tableRef)
      if (!tableSnap.exists()) {
        throw new Error('This table no longer exists — refresh the table list and try again.')
      }
      const capacity = asCount(tableSnap.data().capacity)

      // Read AND write the ledger inside this transaction: it is the shared
      // contention point that serialises two waiters creating sessions for the
      // same table (the loser retries and re-reads everything below).
      const ledgerSnap = await transaction.get(ledgerRef)
      const ledger = (ledgerSnap.exists() ? ledgerSnap.data() : undefined) as CapacityLedger | undefined

      const { occupancy, occupied, activeCount } = await verifyOccupancy(
        transaction,
        database,
        candidateIds,
        ledgerOccupancy(ledger),
      )

      // A capacity of 0 means the legacy document has no usable capacity: the
      // seats cannot be measured, so the existing (uncapped) behaviour is kept
      // rather than hard-blocking a live service.
      if (capacity > 0 && occupied + guests > capacity) {
        throw new SessionCapacityExceededError(capacity, occupied, guests)
      }

      transaction.set(ledgerRef, {
        tableId: session.tableId,
        capacity,
        occupiedGuests: occupied + guests,
        activeSessions: activeCount + 1,
        // Written as a whole map (no merge) so released sessions disappear.
        occupancy: { ...occupancy, [session.id]: guests },
        updatedAt: Date.now(),
      })
      transaction.set(sessionRef, session as unknown as DocumentData)
      // Keeps the physical table marked as in use for every client — the same
      // fields the local state / sync push writes.
      transaction.set(
        tableRef,
        { status: 'occupied', currentSessions: activeCount + 1, updatedAt: Date.now() },
        { merge: true },
      )
    })
    return { authoritative: true }
  } catch (err) {
    if (err instanceof SessionCapacityExceededError) throw err
    if (isOfflineFirestoreError(err)) return { authoritative: false }
    throw err
  }
}

/**
 * Refresh the derived capacity ledger of a table after one of its sessions
 * stopped occupying it (completed / cancelled).
 *
 * The summary is recomputed from the authoritative session documents while
 * ignoring the released session, so it always describes the post-release truth
 * even if the closed status of that session has not reached Firestore yet. It is
 * idempotent and self-healing — it never adds, removes or edits a session.
 */
export const refreshTableCapacityLedger = async (
  tableId: string,
  releasedSessionId: string,
): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  const database = getFirestoreNow()
  if (!database) return

  const tableRef = doc(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.tables, tableId)
  const ledgerRef = doc(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.counters, tableCapacityLedgerId(tableId))

  let candidateIds: string[] = []
  try {
    candidateIds = await discoverOccupyingSessionIds(tableId, database)
  } catch {
    // Offline / unreadable: `reserveSession()` still recomputes the occupancy
    // from the session documents, so this summary may simply stay stale.
    return
  }

  try {
    await runTransaction(database, async (transaction) => {
      // The same document `reserveSession` reads and writes, so a release can
      // never interleave with a concurrent reservation on this table.
      const ledgerSnap = await transaction.get(ledgerRef)
      const tableSnap = await transaction.get(tableRef)
      const capacity = asCount(tableSnap.data()?.capacity)
      const ledger = (ledgerSnap.exists() ? ledgerSnap.data() : undefined) as CapacityLedger | undefined
      const ledgerMap = { ...ledgerOccupancy(ledger) }
      // The released session never occupies the table again — even when its
      // 'closed' status has not reached Firestore yet.
      delete ledgerMap[releasedSessionId]
      const { occupancy, occupied, activeCount } = await verifyOccupancy(
        transaction,
        database,
        candidateIds.filter((id) => id !== releasedSessionId),
        ledgerMap,
      )
      transaction.set(ledgerRef, {
        tableId,
        capacity,
        occupiedGuests: occupied,
        activeSessions: activeCount,
        occupancy,
        updatedAt: Date.now(),
      })
    })
  } catch {
    // Best effort: the ledger is a derived summary and the next reservation
    // recomputes the real occupancy from the session documents.
  }
}

/**
 * Restaurant settings persistence — the ONLY module allowed to write
 * `settings/restaurant`.
 *
 * SAFETY CONTRACT (this is what makes the settings survive restarts):
 *
 *   • Hydration reads Firestore once at startup and treats the document as the
 *     source of truth. Defaults are used ONLY for fields that genuinely do not
 *     exist in the document — an existing document is never written back.
 *   • The document is created once, and only when it truly does not exist.
 *   • Saves write ONLY the fields the operator edited, with `merge: true`, so
 *     unrelated fields in Firestore are always preserved.
 *   • Nothing on a timer / in the sync engine / at startup ever writes the
 *     whole settings object. A complete local object always contains
 *     application defaults, and `setDoc(..., { merge: true })` happily
 *     overwrites existing Firestore fields with those defaults — that is
 *     exactly how production settings used to reset themselves after a
 *     restart, a logout/login or an overnight session.
 */
import { doc, getDoc, onSnapshot, setDoc, type DocumentData } from 'firebase/firestore'
import { getFirestoreNow } from '../../firebase'
import { FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS } from './dataService'
import type { RestaurantSettings } from '../../context/RestaurantContext'

/** Document id used by the application (`settings/restaurant`). */
export const RESTAURANT_SETTINGS_DOC_ID = 'restaurant'

/**
 * Settings fields that must be stored as numbers. Older documents (and past UI
 * builds) could hold them as strings such as `"010"` / `"05"`, which the
 * Settings form then rendered verbatim. They are coerced on hydration so the
 * UI shows `10` and `5`; the coercion is local-only (it never triggers a write).
 */
export const NUMERIC_SETTINGS_FIELDS = [
  'taxRate',
  'serviceCharge',
  'parcelCharge',
  'prepWarningMinutes',
  'printRetryCount',
] as const

export interface SettingsSnapshot {
  /** true when the document exists in Firestore. */
  exists: boolean
  /** Document fields (null when it does not exist or Firestore is unavailable). */
  data: Record<string, unknown> | null
}

const settingsRef = (id: string) => {
  const database = getFirestoreNow()
  return database ? doc(database, FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS.settings, id) : null
}

const describeError = (err: unknown): string => (err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err))

/**
 * `[SETTINGS …]` diagnostics.
 *
 * Deliberately silent: the owner requires a clean browser console, and these
 * calls used to dump the whole settings document. The persistence behaviour is
 * unchanged — the helpers are kept (as no-ops) so every call site stays valid
 * and no settings value is ever written to the console. Real failures are
 * reported through the UI (`settingsHydration === 'error'` / a rejected
 * `updateSettings`) instead of being logged.
 */
export const logSettings = (
  _event: 'INIT' | 'HYDRATED' | 'WRITE' | 'REMOTE' | 'SKIP',
  _detail: string,
): void => {
  void _event
  void _detail
}

export const logSettingsError = (source: string, err: unknown): void => {
  void source
  void err
  void describeError
}


/** Coerce a stored value into a finite number (`"010"` → `10`, `"abc"` → fallback). */
export const toSettingsNumber = (value: unknown, fallback = 0): number => {
  if (typeof value === 'number') return Number.isFinite(value) ? Math.round(value * 100) / 100 : fallback
  if (typeof value === 'string') {
    const cleaned = value.trim().replace(/[^0-9.-]/g, '')
    if (!cleaned) return fallback
    const parsed = Number(cleaned)
    return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? Math.round(parsed * 100) / 100 : fallback
  }
  return fallback
}

/**
 * Firestore values win; `defaults` only fill fields that are absent (or
 * explicitly `undefined`) in the remote document. Never the other way round.
 */
export const withSettingsDefaults = <T extends object>(
  defaults: T,
  remote: Partial<T> | Record<string, unknown> | null | undefined,
): T => {
  const merged: Record<string, unknown> = { ...(defaults as Record<string, unknown>) }
  if (remote) {
    for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(remote)) {
      if (value === undefined) continue
      merged[key] = value
    }
  }
  return merged as T
}

/** Numeric fields coerced to numbers (display/state normalisation only). */
export const normalizeSettingsNumbers = <T extends object>(settings: T): T => {
  const normalized: Record<string, unknown> = { ...(settings as Record<string, unknown>) }
  for (const field of NUMERIC_SETTINGS_FIELDS) {
    if (field in normalized) normalized[field] = toSettingsNumber(normalized[field], 0)
  }
  return normalized as T
}

/** Drop `undefined` values so a merge patch never erases an existing field. */
export const buildSettingsPatch = (data: Partial<RestaurantSettings>): Record<string, unknown> => {
  const patch: Record<string, unknown> = {}
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(data)) {
    if (value === undefined) continue
    patch[key] = (NUMERIC_SETTINGS_FIELDS as readonly string[]).includes(key)
      ? toSettingsNumber(value, 0)
      : value
  }
  return patch
}

/** Read the settings document once (no side effects). */
export const readRestaurantSettings = async (
  id: string = RESTAURANT_SETTINGS_DOC_ID,
): Promise<SettingsSnapshot> => {
  const ref = settingsRef(id)
  if (!ref) return { exists: false, data: null }
  const snap = await getDoc(ref)
  return { exists: snap.exists(), data: snap.exists() ? (snap.data() as Record<string, unknown>) : null }
}


/**
 * Create `settings/<id>` exactly once with the supplied defaults. Returns
 * `created: false` when the document already exists — an existing document is
 * NEVER touched by this function.
 */
export const createRestaurantSettingsIfMissing = async (
  defaults: Partial<RestaurantSettings>,
  id: string = RESTAURANT_SETTINGS_DOC_ID,
): Promise<{ created: boolean; data: Record<string, unknown> | null }> => {
  const ref = settingsRef(id)
  if (!ref) return { created: false, data: null }
  const current = await getDoc(ref)
  if (current.exists()) return { created: false, data: current.data() as Record<string, unknown> }
  const payload = buildSettingsPatch(defaults)
  if (Object.keys(payload).length === 0) return { created: false, data: null }
  await setDoc(ref, payload as DocumentData, { merge: true })
  return { created: true, data: payload }
}

/**
 * Write ONLY the edited fields into `settings/<id>` (`merge: true`). Every other
 * field that already exists in Firestore is left untouched. Rejects when
 * Firestore rejects, so callers never report success for a failed write.
 */
export const writeRestaurantSettingsPatch = async (
  patch: Record<string, unknown>,
  id: string = RESTAURANT_SETTINGS_DOC_ID,
): Promise<void> => {
  const ref = settingsRef(id)
  if (!ref) throw new Error('Firebase Firestore is unavailable.')
  const payload = buildSettingsPatch(patch as Partial<RestaurantSettings>)
  if (Object.keys(payload).length === 0) return
  await setDoc(ref, payload as DocumentData, { merge: true })
}

/**
 * Live, read-only subscription to the settings document. Keeps every open
 * session (admin, supervisor, waiter) in sync with the values that are actually
 * stored — without it a long-running session keeps stale values and can revert
 * another admin's change.
 */
export const watchRestaurantSettings = (
  onChange: (snapshot: SettingsSnapshot) => void,
  id: string = RESTAURANT_SETTINGS_DOC_ID,
): (() => void) => {
  const ref = settingsRef(id)
  if (!ref) return () => {}
  return onSnapshot(
    ref,
    (snap) =>
      onChange({
        exists: snap.exists(),
        data: snap.exists() ? (snap.data() as Record<string, unknown>) : null,
      }),
    (err) => logSettingsError('watchRestaurantSettings', err),
  )
}

// Firebase Storage service for dish / profile images.
// Stores the file in Firebase Storage and returns { imageUrl, imagePath }.
// Only the URL/path is persisted to Firestore — never base64.
import { ref, uploadBytes, getDownloadURL, deleteObject } from 'firebase/storage'
import { getStorageNow } from '../../firebase'
import { isFirebaseConfigured } from './config'

/** Storage path: restaurants/{restaurantId}/menu/{menuItemId}/original */
export const getMenuImagePath = (restaurantId: string, menuItemId: string): string =>
  `restaurants/${restaurantId}/menu/${menuItemId}/original`

export const getMemberImagePath = (userId: string): string => `members/${userId}/avatar`

export interface UploadResult {
  imageUrl: string
  imagePath: string
}

/**
 * A URL that survives a reload and is visible on every device.
 *
 * `data:` URLs (base64 previews) and `blob:` object URLs exist only inside the
 * browser tab that created them: they must NEVER be written to Firestore (a
 * base64 payload has no business in a document, and both break on the next
 * reload / on another device). Image forms use this to decide whether a value
 * can be persisted as-is.
 */
export const isDurableImageUrl = (url?: string): boolean =>
  !!url && !url.startsWith('data:') && !url.startsWith('blob:')

const fileToBytes = async (file: File): Promise<Uint8Array> => new Uint8Array(await file.arrayBuffer())

export const uploadMenuImage = async (file: File, restaurantId: string, menuItemId: string): Promise<UploadResult> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured. Set VITE_DATA_MODE=mock or provide Firebase credentials.')
  const storage = getStorageNow()
  if (!storage) throw new Error('Firebase Storage is unavailable. Check the Firebase configuration.')
  const path = getMenuImagePath(restaurantId, menuItemId)
  const storageRef = ref(storage, path)
  await uploadBytes(storageRef, await fileToBytes(file), { contentType: file.type })
  const imageUrl = await getDownloadURL(storageRef)
  return { imageUrl, imagePath: path }
}

export const uploadMemberImage = async (file: File, userId: string): Promise<UploadResult> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured.')
  const storage = getStorageNow()
  if (!storage) throw new Error('Firebase Storage is unavailable. Check the Firebase configuration.')
  const path = getMemberImagePath(userId)
  const storageRef = ref(storage, path)
  await uploadBytes(storageRef, await fileToBytes(file), { contentType: file.type })
  const imageUrl = await getDownloadURL(storageRef)
  return { imageUrl, imagePath: path }
}

export const deleteMenuImage = async (imagePath: string): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  const storage = getStorageNow()
  if (!storage) throw new Error('Firebase Storage is unavailable. Check the Firebase configuration.')
  await deleteObject(ref(storage, imagePath))
}

/** Delete a member's profile photo (best-effort; missing objects are ignored). */
export const deleteMemberImage = async (imagePath: string): Promise<void> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return
  const storage = getStorageNow()
  if (!storage) throw new Error('Firebase Storage is unavailable. Check the Firebase configuration.')
  try {
    await deleteObject(ref(storage, imagePath))
  } catch (err) {
    const code = (err as { code?: string })?.code
    if (code === 'storage/object-not-found') return
    throw err
  }
}

export const getImageUrl = async (imagePath: string): Promise<string> => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) throw new Error('Firebase is not configured.')
  const storage = getStorageNow()
  if (!storage) throw new Error('Firebase Storage is unavailable. Check the Firebase configuration.')
  return getDownloadURL(ref(storage, imagePath))
}

/**
 * Firestore sync engine (offline-first).
 *
 * Responsibilities:
 *   • hydrate every business collection from Firestore once, then keep it live
 *     with `onSnapshot` (a token confirmed on a waiter's phone appears on the
 *     admin dashboard within a second — on ANY device);
 *   • treat the server snapshot as the source of truth for deletes, while never
 *     losing records created on this device while offline;
 *   • push only the entities that actually changed, debounced, in chunked
 *     batches — so a busy service never fires hundreds of Firestore writes and
 *     the UI never blocks;
 *   • respect the per-role write matrix (identical to firestore.rules) so a
 *     waiter never attempts a write the rules would reject.
 *
 * The engine is framework-free; the React context owns state and simply tells
 * it "something changed" via `schedule()`.
 */
import { dataMode, isFirebaseConfigured } from './config'
import { loadCollection, saveEntities, watchCollection } from './dataService'
import type { DirectoryRole } from './userService'

export interface SyncEntity {
  id: string
  createdAt?: number
  updatedAt?: number
  timestamp?: number
  startTime?: number
  generatedAt?: number
  recordedAt?: number
}

export interface SyncBinding {
  /** Firestore collection name (see FIRESTORE_COLLECTIONS). */
  name: string
  /** Current local items (reads live state through a ref). */
  read: () => unknown[]
  /** Apply an authoritative remote snapshot to React state. */
  write: (items: unknown[]) => void
}

export interface SyncEngine {
  /** Queue a debounced push after local state changed. */
  schedule: () => void
  /** Stop listeners + timers (provider unmount). */
  stop: () => void
}

/** Which roles may write each collection — mirrors firestore.rules exactly. */
const WRITE_MATRIX: Record<string, DirectoryRole[]> = {
  orders: ['admin', 'waiter', 'supervisor'],
  diningSessions: ['admin', 'waiter', 'supervisor'],
  tables: ['admin', 'waiter', 'supervisor'],
  menu: ['admin', 'supervisor'],
  menuCategories: ['admin', 'supervisor'],
  // Billing & payments are admin-only (see firestore.rules). Waiters read their
  // session bill/payment status but cannot write or alter them.
  bills: ['admin'],
  paymentRecords: ['admin'],
  notifications: ['admin', 'waiter', 'supervisor'],
  inventory: ['admin', 'supervisor'],
  stockHistory: ['admin', 'supervisor'],
  inventoryUsage: ['admin', 'supervisor'],
  purchaseRequests: ['admin', 'supervisor'],
  recipes: ['admin', 'supervisor'],
  activityLog: ['admin', 'waiter', 'supervisor'],
}

export const canWriteCollection = (name: string, role?: DirectoryRole): boolean =>
  role != null && (WRITE_MATRIX[name]?.includes(role) ?? false)

/** Only admins may delete (Firestore rules enforce the same). */
export const canDeleteCollection = (name: string, role?: DirectoryRole): boolean =>
  role === 'admin' && canWriteCollection(name, role)

/** Best-effort timestamp of an entity, used for newest-first ordering + freshness. */
export const stampOf = (entity: SyncEntity): number =>
  entity.createdAt ??
  entity.timestamp ??
  entity.generatedAt ??
  entity.recordedAt ??
  entity.updatedAt ??
  entity.startTime ??
  0

interface CollectionState {
  ref: unknown
  pushed: Map<string, string>
  dirty: boolean
  pending: { ids: Set<string>; at: number } | null
  /** Hydration finished (or failed) — only then may local state be pushed. */
  ready: boolean
}

export interface SyncEngineOptions {
  /** Current signed-in role (read through a getter so it stays fresh). */
  role: () => DirectoryRole | undefined
  bindings: SyncBinding[]
}

const PUSH_DEBOUNCE_MS = 350
const SHIELD_MS = 20_000
/** Automatic retry delay while a collection still has unpushed changes. */
const PUSH_RETRY_MS = 5_000

/**
 * Page-load timestamp. `offlineNew` protection used to be scoped to a single
 * engine instance, but the engine restarts whenever the auth identity object
 * changes (ID-token refresh / directory sync). Records created earlier in the
 * SAME page session but not yet durable on the server were then dropped by the
 * re-hydration and could never be pushed — they "disappeared" on the next
 * reload. Anchoring the window to the page load keeps them until they land,
 * while state from a PREVIOUS page load is never kept (firebase mode boots
 * empty by design).
 */
const APP_SESSION_START = Date.now()

export const startFirebaseSync = (options: SyncEngineOptions): SyncEngine => {
  if (dataMode !== 'firebase' || !isFirebaseConfigured()) {
    return { schedule: () => {}, stop: () => {} }
  }

  const states = new Map<string, CollectionState>()
  const stateFor = (name: string): CollectionState => {
    let state = states.get(name)
    if (!state) {
      state = { ref: null, pushed: new Map(), dirty: false, pending: null, ready: false }
      states.set(name, state)
    }
    return state
  }

  let stopped = false
  const unsubscribers: (() => void)[] = []

  /** Adopt a server snapshot: authoritative for deletes, tolerant for offline-new items. */
  const applyRemote = (binding: SyncBinding, remote: SyncEntity[]): void => {
    const state = stateFor(binding.name)
    if (state.pending) {
      const landed = [...state.pending.ids].every((id) => remote.some((r) => r.id === id))
      const expired = Date.now() - state.pending.at > SHIELD_MS
      // Our own write has not reached the server yet — the snapshot is stale and
      // applying it would visibly revert the operator's action.
      if (!landed && !expired) return
      state.pending = null
    }
    const remoteIds = new Set(remote.map((r) => r.id))
    const offlineNew = (binding.read() as SyncEntity[]).filter(
      (item) => !remoteIds.has(item.id) && stampOf(item) >= APP_SESSION_START,
    )
    const merged = [...remote, ...offlineNew].sort((a, b) => stampOf(b) - stampOf(a))
    state.pushed = new Map(remote.map((r) => [r.id, JSON.stringify(r)]))
    state.ref = merged
    state.dirty = offlineNew.length > 0
    state.ready = true
    binding.write(merged)
  }

  // ── 1. One-time hydration so nothing flashes empty on load ────────────────
  // Firestore is ALWAYS authoritative: an empty collection means "empty", it
  // does NOT mean "seed the database with whatever this browser happens to
  // hold". `applyRemote` still keeps entities that were genuinely created
  // during THIS session (see `offlineNew`), so a record the operator created
  // while offline is never lost — while stale in-memory/default state can
  // never be pushed as production data.
  options.bindings.forEach((binding) => {
    void loadCollection<SyncEntity>(binding.name)
      .then((remote) => {
        if (stopped) return
        applyRemote(binding, remote)
      })
      .catch((err) => {
        // Hydration failed (offline / rules). Mark the collection ready so the
        // operator's own local edits can still be retried later instead of
        // being blocked forever; the live listener below recovers as soon as
        // Firestore answers again. The failure itself is logged truthfully —
        // a silent drop here is how records vanish between days.
        stateFor(binding.name).ready = true
        console.error(
          `Firestore hydration failed for "${binding.name}":`,
          err instanceof Error ? err.message : err,
        )
      })
  })

  // ── 2. Live listeners: any device's change lands here in real time ────────
  options.bindings.forEach((binding) => {
    unsubscribers.push(
      watchCollection<SyncEntity>(binding.name, (remote) => {
        if (!stopped) applyRemote(binding, remote)
      }),
    )
  })

  // ── 3. Settings document (settings/restaurant) ───────────────────────────
  //
  // NOTHING here. Settings are deliberately NOT part of the background push:
  // the local settings object always contains application defaults, so pushing
  // it (even with `merge: true`) overwrites real Firestore values. A stale,
  // un-hydrated or long-running admin session therefore used to reset the
  // restaurant settings overnight. Settings are now written ONLY by an explicit
  // admin save, field-by-field (see services/firebase/settingsService.ts), and
  // are hydrated + watched separately in RestaurantContext.

  // ── 4. Debounced diff push ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  let timer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null
  let retryTimer: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | null = null
  let running = false
  let queued = false

  const pushAll = async (): Promise<void> => {
    const role = options.role()
    for (const binding of options.bindings) {
      if (stopped) return
      const state = stateFor(binding.name)
      const items = binding.read() as SyncEntity[]
      // Wait for hydration so a stale local cache can never overwrite Firestore.
      if (!state.ready) continue
      // Fast path: state untouched since the last successful push.
      if (state.ref === items && !state.dirty) continue
      if (!canWriteCollection(binding.name, role)) {
        state.ref = items
        continue
      }
      const next = new Map<string, string>()
      const upserts: SyncEntity[] = []
      for (const item of items) {
        const json = JSON.stringify(item)
        next.set(item.id, json)
        if (state.pushed.get(item.id) !== json) upserts.push(item)
      }
      const deletes: string[] = []
      if (canDeleteCollection(binding.name, role)) {
        for (const id of state.pushed.keys()) if (!next.has(id)) deletes.push(id)
      }
      if (upserts.length === 0 && deletes.length === 0) {
        state.ref = items
        continue
      }
      state.pending = { ids: new Set([...upserts.map((u) => u.id), ...deletes]), at: Date.now() }
      try {
        await saveEntities(binding.name, upserts, deletes)
        state.pushed = next
        state.ref = items
        state.dirty = false
      } catch (err) {
        // Surface the failure truthfully and keep the collection dirty so the
        // automatic retry below replays the SAME diff. Swallowing this error
        // silently was how a record could appear on screen yet never reach
        // Firestore — and be gone after the next reload.
        console.error(
          `Firestore push failed for "${binding.name}":`,
          err instanceof Error ? err.message : err,
        )
        state.dirty = true
        state.pending = null
      }
    }

  }

  /**
   * While any collection still has unpushed changes, retry automatically.
   * Previously a failed push waited indefinitely for some unrelated state
   * change (or a tab visibility event) before it was ever attempted again.
   */
  const scheduleRetryIfNeeded = (): void => {
    if (stopped || retryTimer || timer) return
    const anyDirty = options.bindings.some((binding) => stateFor(binding.name).dirty)
    if (!anyDirty) return
    retryTimer = setTimeout(() => {
      retryTimer = null
      void run()
    }, PUSH_RETRY_MS)
  }

  const run = async (): Promise<void> => {
    if (running) {
      queued = true
      return
    }
    running = true
    try {
      await pushAll()
    } catch (err) {
        if (import.meta.env.DEV) console.error('Firestore sync push failed:', err instanceof Error ? err.message : err)
    } finally {
      running = false
      if (queued) {
        queued = false
        await run()
      } else {
        scheduleRetryIfNeeded()
      }
    }
  }

  const schedule = (): void => {
    if (stopped || timer) return
    timer = setTimeout(() => {
      timer = null
      void run()
    }, PUSH_DEBOUNCE_MS)
  }

  // Anything still unpushed when the tab is closed or hidden is flushed now.
  const flushNow = () => {
    if (timer) {
      clearTimeout(timer)
      timer = null
    }
    void run()
  }
  document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', flushNow)
  window.addEventListener('beforeunload', flushNow)

  const stop = () => {
    stopped = true
    if (timer) clearTimeout(timer)
    if (retryTimer) {
      clearTimeout(retryTimer)
      retryTimer = null
    }
    document.removeEventListener('visibilitychange', flushNow)
    window.removeEventListener('beforeunload', flushNow)
    unsubscribers.forEach((unsub) => unsub())
  }

  return { schedule, stop }
}

/**
 * Firestore atomic token counter — one document per (series, restaurant day):
 *   counters/tokens_{series}_{YYYY-MM-DD}  →  { value: number }
 *
 * Uses a Firestore transaction so two waiters on two different phones can never
 * receive the same token. Dine-in and parcel run on SEPARATE series, matching the
 * mock-mode numbering (and the `P-###` parcel labels).
 *
 * The document id is deliberately a flat `counters/*` doc: the previous
 * `counters/tokens/{date}` sub-collection path was not reachable by the
 * deployed security rules, so every token mint failed in Firebase mode.
 */
import { runTransaction, doc, getDoc } from 'firebase/firestore'
import { getFirestoreNow } from '../../firebase'
import { isFirebaseConfigured } from './config'

export type TokenSeries = 'dine_in' | 'parcel'

/** Stable Firestore doc id for a series/day pair (also used by the config checker). */
export const tokenCounterId = (series: TokenSeries, dateKey: string): string =>
  `tokens_${series}_${dateKey}`

const counterRef = (series: TokenSeries, dateKey: string) => {
  if (!isFirebaseConfigured()) return null
  const database = getFirestoreNow()
  if (!database) return null
  return doc(database, 'counters', tokenCounterId(series, dateKey))
}

/** Atomic next token for the restaurant day. Throws when Firestore is unavailable. */
export const nextToken = async (dateKey: string, series: TokenSeries = 'dine_in'): Promise<number> => {
  const database = getFirestoreNow()
  const ref = counterRef(series, dateKey)
  if (!database || !ref) throw new Error('Firestore is not configured')
  let assigned = 0
  await runTransaction(database, async (transaction) => {
    const snap = await transaction.get(ref)
    const current = (snap.exists() && Number(snap.data().value)) || 0
    assigned = current + 1
    transaction.set(ref, { value: assigned, series, date: dateKey, updatedAt: Date.now() })
  })
  return assigned
}

/** Read the current token value for a day without incrementing. */
export const currentToken = async (dateKey: string, series: TokenSeries = 'dine_in'): Promise<number> => {
  const ref = counterRef(series, dateKey)
  if (!ref) return 0
  const snap = await getDoc(ref)
  return snap.exists() ? Number(snap.data().value) : 0
}
